Мы за тебя готовы пройти сквозь сталь и пламя, Румыния, веди нас, сражаться нам вели! Пусть тех, кто сердцем будет с коварными врагами, Господь огнём и серой сотрет с лица земли! Довольно мы страдали от черных ятаганов, нам не страшны удары позорного кнута. Вставайте же, румыны! Долой ярмо тиранов! Свобода, честь отчизны навек для нас свята. Пусть враг нас хочет сделать скотиной бессловесной, похитить речь родную и мудрость наших книг, на смертный бой пойдем мы, ряды смыкая тесно, и не пленит захватчик свободный наш язык! Сыны земли румынской, забудем разногласья, единой силой встанем за милый отчий край, и о злодействе новом заявим громогласно: в руках убийц коварных великий наш Дунай! Благословенна будет грядущая расплата, священный, вечный подвиг — спасти страну свою. Мы вызволим отчизну из рабства супостатов или падем со славой в отчаянном бою!

Diane Crump (May 18, 1948 – January 1, 2026) was an American jockey and horse trainer. On February 7, 1969, she became the first woman to compete as a professional jockey in a pari-mutuel race in the United States, riding a horse named Bridle 'n Bit at Hialeah Park Race Track. Her participation faced intense hostility, requiring a full police escort through an angry crowd of shouting people, with hecklers yelling things like "Go back to the kitchen and cook dinner." Crump finished 9th in the 12-horse race and later recalled that her excitement allowed her to overcome the negative attitudes of male jockeys, trainers, and owners. Two weeks later, she won her first race. She was inspired to apply for a jockey's license in the fall of 1968 after Kathryn Kusner, the first woman licensed as a jockey, won a lawsuit against the Maryland Racing Commission for gender-based denial of a license; although Kusner was injured shortly after receiving her license, Crump stepped forward. Throughout 1968, female jockeys faced significant resistance; for example, W. L. Lyons Brown, a part owner of Churchill Downs, requested Crump not compete there due to anticipated controversy, and Penny Ann Early was denied the chance to ride because male jockeys boycotted her races. Two other women had been forced out of races after male jockeys threw rocks at their trailers and threatened a boycott. The situation at Hialeah changed when track officials threatened sanctions against male jockeys. In 1970, Crump became the first woman to ride in the Kentucky Derby, winning the first race on the undercard and finishing 15th in a 17-horse field on a horse named Fathom. By the time she retired from racing in 1985, she had ridden to 235 wins, though Equibase officially credits her with 228. She received invitations to ride in Puerto Rico and Venezuela; in a 1970s Puerto Rican race, she hit a male jockey with her whip after he held onto her saddle, and he eventually pulled away to win. On February 1, 1989, Crump suffered a serious riding accident in which she was crushed under her horse, breaking her leg in six or seven places, her ankle, and ribs, requiring ten days in the hospital and leading doctors to say she would never ride again. After recovery, she returned to riding, but accumulated injuries over the years ultimately led to her permanent retirement in 1999. She briefly retired in 1985 to focus on family, working as a farm trainer at Calumet Farm in Lexington, Kentucky, for over three years, and later trained horses at the Middleburg Training Center in Virginia starting in 1991. She resumed riding in 1992 and competed through 1998 before retiring in 1999. She ran an equine sales business and lived in Virginia. Crump was married to trainer Don Divine from 1969 to 1987. In 2020, a biography titled Diane Crump: A Horse Racing Pioneer's Life in the Saddle by Mark Shrager was published. In 2025, she was diagnosed with glioblastoma, and her family launched a GoFundMe to cover medical expenses. She died on January 1, 2026, in Winchester, Virginia, at the age of 77.

Richard Huemer (January 2, 1898 – November 30, 1979) was an American animator active during the Golden Age of Animation. While working as an artist-illustrator in the Bronx, New York City, he began his animation career at the Raoul Barré cartoon studio in 1916. In 1923, he joined the Fleischer Studio, where he developed the Koko the Clown character, redesigned the clown for more efficient animation, and reduced the studio’s reliance on the Rotoscope for smooth motion. He created Ko-Ko's canine companion, Fitz, and established the drawing style that defined the series. After moving to Hollywood, Huemer worked as an animator and director at the Charles Mintz studio, where he developed the character Scrappy. He later joined the Disney Studio, remaining there from April 16, 1933, to February 28, 1973, with a three-year break from 1948 to 1951 during which he pioneered animated TV commercials and co-created with Paul Murry the comic strip The Adventures of Buck O'Rue. Huemer collaborated extensively with Joe Grant on several projects, including Fantasia (as story director), Dumbo (as screenplay), and various propaganda films supporting the U.S. war effort in World War II. Notably, Huemer and Grant submitted Dumbo to Walt Disney not as a completed storyboard, but as a series of storyboard "chapters" ending in cliffhangers, a strategy that successfully generated Disney’s interest in the project. In February 1973, Huemer was presented with a Mousecar by the Disney Studio during a ceremony attended by fellow animators. He received the Winsor McCay Award at the Annie Awards in October 1978, introduced by Ward Kimball. On October 10, 2007, Huemer's son, Dr. Richard P. Huemer, accepted the Disney Legends award in his father's name.

This discography outlines the musical works of the German rock band Die Toten Hosen, including their pseudonyms Die Roten Rosen and Tangobrüder. The band has sold more than 18 million records, with certified sales exceeding 14.5 million units in Germany, establishing them as one of the country’s best-selling music acts. Their most successful release is the compilation album Reich & sexy, which has sold over 1.1 million copies. Both Reich & sexy and their ninth studio album Opium fürs Volk became million-sellers in Germany and are among the best-selling albums of the 1990s in the country. The video album Nur zu Besuch: Unplugged im Wiener Burgtheater, with over 100,000 copies sold, is one of the best-selling video albums in Germany. By September 2023, the band had released 15 studio albums and eight live albums, along with nine compilation albums, three of which were produced for international markets. Among these, Love, Peace & Money and Crash-Landing are collections of the band’s songs featuring newly written English lyrics. Beyond these, they have released more than 70 singles and two EPs. The members have also contributed to albums by other artists, appeared on numerous compilations, and participated in radio, television, and film productions as guest musicians or extras. Eight songbooks containing sheet music and lyrics have been published. By December 2017, the band had released a total of 365 original compositions and over 168 cover versions. To mark their 30th anniversary, the studio album Ballast der Republik was released in May 2012 and immediately reached number one in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. In May 2017, the band achieved their tenth number-one album in Germany with Laune der Natur; by now, that number has risen to twelve, making them one of the most successful musicians in the German-speaking world. The band’s first charting album was released in 1987 under the pseudonym Die Roten Rosen, titled Never Mind The Hosen – Here’s Die Roten Rosen. In 1990, Auf dem Kreuzzug ins Glück became their first studio album to reach number one in the German charts. With Auswärtsspiel in 2002, the band topped the Austrian charts for the first time. Their most commercially successful single until 2012 was Zehn kleine Jägermeister (1996), which reached number one in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland and was certified platinum in Germany for over 500,000 sales. In 2012, the single Tage wie diese reached number one on the German Singles Chart and sold more than 990,000 copies across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since their formation in 1982, Die Toten Hosen have maintained almost the same lineup: Campino on vocals, Andreas von Holst and Michael Breitkopf on guitars, and Andreas Meurer on bass. There was one drummer change in 1986, when founding member Trini Trimpop was replaced by Wolfgang Rohde, who remained with the band until 1999, alternating with Vom Ritchie on the album Unsterblich, where he appears on only four tracks. Vom Ritchie then took over permanently as the group’s drummer. All albums from 1982 to 2005 were produced by Jon Caffery, except for Never Mind The Hosen – Here’s Die Roten Rosen, which the band produced themselves. Starting with the album In aller Stille in 2008, Vincent Sorg has been responsible for producing their music. Die Toten Hosen produced their first two singles and debut album Opel-Gang on their own label, Totenkopf, which was managed by Jochen Hülder and Trini Trimpop. Hülder remained the band’s manager until his death in 2015. In 1983, the band signed with EMI, which financed the video for Eisgekühlter Bommerlunder and a concert tour. However, they switched to Virgin Records in 1984 with the release of Unter falscher Flagge, remaining with the label until 1995. Since the expiration of their contract with Virgin and the release of Opium fürs Volk, the band has issued all their releases through their own label, JKP.

Different World is the debut studio album by Norwegian DJ and record producer Alan Walker, released on 14 December 2018 through MER Musikk and Sony Music Entertainment, and includes his successful 2015 single "Faded". The album follows a trilogy of singles titled World of Walker, consisting of "All Falls Down", "Darkside", and "Diamond Heart". It was nominated for Top Dance/Electronic Albums at the 2020 Billboard Music Awards. Featuring artists such as Steve Aoki, Noah Cyrus, and Digital Farm Animals, the album combines recognizable tracks like "Faded" with new material such as "Lost Control". Walker stated that releasing the album was an "incredible feeling" and described it as a significant milestone after years of work, expressing excitement to share it with fans. A campaign titled "#CreateADifferentWorld" was launched to raise awareness about climate change. The first single, "Faded", features uncredited Naustdal pop singer Iselin Solheim and was released on 3 December 2015; it reached number one in Austria, Germany, Switzerland, and Sweden, was nominated for British Single of the Year at the 2017 Brit Awards, and won Årets Låt (Song of the Year) at the Spellemannprisen. The second single, "Sing Me to Sleep", also featuring Iselin Solheim, was released on June 3, 2016, and reached number one in Norway and number one on the iTunes charts in seven countries. "Alone", featuring uncredited singer Noonie Bao, was released as the third single on December 2, 2016, and charted internationally, reaching number one on the Norwegian Singles Chart. "All Falls Down", featuring Noah Cyrus and Digital Farm Animals, was released as the fourth single on 27 October 2017 and peaked at number one on the Norwegian Singles Chart and the US Billboard Dance Club Songs chart. "Darkside", featuring Antiguan-German singer-songwriter Au/Ra and Norwegian singer Tomine Harket, was released as the fifth single on 27 July 2018, with a remix by Dutch DJ Afrojack that reached number one in Norway and number 10 in Sweden. "Diamond Heart", featuring Swedish singer-songwriter Sophia Somajo, was released as the sixth single on September 28, 2018, with official remixes by Syn Cole and Dzeko; its music video was nominated for Best Cinematography at the 2019 Berlin Music Video Awards. "Different World", featuring American singer Sofia Carson, Norwegian music producer K-391, and Chinese music producer Corsak, was released as the album's lead single on November 30, 2018, coinciding with the "#CreateADifferentWorld" campaign and includes Walker's commentary on climate change; it reached number 31 in the Norwegian charts. Dancing Astronaut described the album as extending the fullest portrait of Walker's distinctive sound and a tightly threaded collection of songs that showcases his sonic artistry. Billboard called it a project that turns bleating synth melodies into sing-alongs, melts warm Caribbean rhythms with hardstyle booms, and electrifies the dance floor while aiming for radio readiness. Manuel Probst of Dance-Charts [de] noted that Walker's typical sound design runs through the album like a common thread, creating a melancholy atmosphere with attention to detail allowing each song to have a unique touch. Marit Johansen Jegthaug of NRK P3 criticized the album for having too few new songs, poor structure, lack of variety, and a lack of distinction between old and new tracks. Tor Martin Bøe of Verdens Gang gave it a "die throw" rating of 3 out of 6, describing it as "manic and gloomy" and stating the dark sense of abandonment feels "almost tacked on". Anjali Raguraman of The Straits Times described it as a "cinematic, vocals-driven album" and noted that it feels like Walker has played it safe by sticking to his familiar style. At the time of Billboard's 2019 mid-year report, the album had 93,000 equivalent album sales in the United States and "Faded" had 192,396,000 streams. Sales figures are based on certification alone; sales+streaming figures are also based on certification alone.

Dina Nath Walli (1908–2006), also known by his pen name Almast Kashmiri, was an Indian watercolour artist and poet from Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley. He was a key figure in the modern art movement in Jammu and Kashmir and is recognized for painting everyday scenes of Kashmir. Born in 1906 in the Badyar Bala neighborhood of Srinagar, within the then princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, part of British India, he belonged to a Kashmiri Pandit family; his father passed away when he was very young. He received his early education in Srinagar and later completed a three-year course at Amar Singh Technical Institute, Srinagar, before moving to Calcutta in the Bengal Presidency in 1930 for further artistic training, where he studied various art forms under Percy Brown, the principal of the Government College of Art & Craft at the University of Calcutta. In 1936, he returned to Srinagar and focused on landscape painting in watercolours. He was awarded gold medals by the government of Kashmir in 1939 and received a highly commended medal from the Academy of Fine Arts, Calcutta in 1940. He also produced an album containing 12 paintings. Under the pen name Almast Kashmiri, his emphasis on realistic art and people's poetry is evident in his two poetry collections: Bala Yapair (This side of Mountains, 1955) and Sahaavukh Posh (Desert Flowers, 1981).

doc_name: Disappearance and murder of Gannon Stauch
text: Gannon Stauch (September 29, 2008 – January 27, 2020) was an American boy who was murdered by his stepmother, Letecia Hardin (then Stauch), in Colorado Springs, Colorado. His disappearance and death drew national attention and prompted a large-scale search effort involving multiple law enforcement agencies and volunteers. Gannon was reported missing by his stepmother on January 27, 2020, when she told the El Paso County Sheriff's Office that he had left home between 3:15 p.m. and 4 p.m. to walk to a friend's house but never returned. The initial press release described him as a "juvenile runaway," but three days later, the sheriff’s office reclassified the case as a missing or endangered person due to new information. The search involved thousands of hours of investigation and hundreds of public tips, with assistance from the FBI Child Abduction Rapid Deployment team, the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, and the Colorado Springs Police Department. Search teams used drones, dogs, horses, helicopters, and divers to search various areas. Gannon's biological parents made emotional pleas for his safe return and thanked the community for their support. On March 2, 2020, Letecia Stauch was arrested in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, on charges of first-degree murder of a child by a person in a position of trust, child abuse resulting in death, tampering with a deceased human body, and tampering with physical evidence. She was extradited to Colorado and held without bond at the El Paso County jail. According to the arrest affidavit released on May 5, 2020, Letecia Stauch killed Gannon in his bedroom on the day he went missing, stabbing him 18 times, hitting him in the head with an object, and shooting him with a handgun. She then cleaned up the crime scene and disposed of his body in a suitcase, lying to investigators about her whereabouts and activities. She claimed Gannon was sick and stayed home from school, and drove with him to various places, but surveillance footage showed she left home with Gannon in her truck around 10:15 a.m. and returned with him around 2:19 p.m. On March 17, 2020, Gannon's remains were found by a maintenance worker under Escambia Bay Bridge in Pace, Florida, more than 1,300 miles from his home. The cause of death was blunt force trauma, sharp force injuries, and a gunshot wound. Investigators believe Letecia Stauch transported his body to Florida by driving there in a rented van after initially dumping it in a remote location north of Colorado Springs and retrieving it later. Letecia Stauch pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity and claimed she had dissociative identity disorder due to childhood sexual abuse. She also accused her husband of being involved in Gannon's death, alleging he had connections to drug cartels and sex trafficking rings, but was found competent to stand trial by a state mental hospital and her claims were dismissed by the court as unfounded. Her five-week trial concluded on May 8, 2023, with the prosecution presenting testimonies from Gannon's father, Letecia's former employers, family, investigators, forensic experts, and state psychiatrists. The defense offered Dorothy Otnow Lewis, a controversial psychiatrist specializing in dissociative identity disorder, as their sole witness. The jury rejected both the insanity defense and Otnow Lewis' testimony, and Letecia Stauch was found guilty of all charges. On the same day, she was sentenced to life in prison without parole plus 156 years by Judge Gregory Werner, who described her actions as “the most horrific I have ever seen” and stated she deserved “the maximum sentence that I can impose according to Colorado law.”

Disney Channel is an American pay television channel and the flagship property of Disney Branded Television, a unit of the Disney Entertainment business segment of the Walt Disney Company. Launched on April 18, 1983, as The Disney Channel as a premium channel on top of basic cable, it initially targeted families due to the availability of home television sets at the time. It dropped "The" from its name in 1997, rebranding as Disney Channel, shifting its focus to children and adolescents aged 6–14. The channel broadcasts original first-run children's television series, theatrically released and original television films, and selected third-party programming. As of November 2023, it is available to approximately 70 million pay television households in the United States, down from its peak of 100 million in 2011. Its international footprint, which once included 46 channels in 33 languages, has declined in parts of Europe and most of the Asia-Pacific due to the launch of Disney+ and competition from streaming and social media platforms. The channel launched nationally at 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time on April 18, 1983, under The Disney Channel, with founding president Alan Wagner helping to develop it; it became available in all 50 U.S. states by September 1983 and reached over 611,000 subscribers by December 1983. It debuted its first made-for-cable movie, Tiger Town, in October 1983, earning a CableACE Award, and achieved profitability by January 1985, with 1.75 million subscribers by that time. In September 1990, TCI's Montgomery, Alabama, system became the first to carry it as a basic cable service. Between 1991 and 1996, more cable providers transitioned it from a premium add-on to a basic tier, though Walt Disney Company executives denied plans to convert it into an ad-supported basic service, calling the shift part of a five-year "hybrid" strategy. On April 6, 1997, it officially rebranded as Disney Channel, though it was occasionally marketed as "Disney" from 1997 to 2002. Television films were produced under Disney Channel Premiere Films starting with Tiger Town in 1983, until October 1997, when the label was replaced with "Disney Channel Original Movies" (DCOM), with the first DCOM being Under Wraps, which premiered on October 25, 1997. The most successful DCOM in terms of popularity and accolades is High School Musical 2, which debuted on August 17, 2007, to 17.2 million viewers, setting a longstanding record for the highest-rated television premiere on the channel. Following it, the second-highest-rated DCOM premieres were Wizards of Waverly Place: The Movie, Camp Rock, Descendants 2, Princess Protection Program, Teen Beach Movie, and Jump In!. It previously held the record for the most-watched basic cable program until December 3, 2007, when ESPN surpassed it with an NFL game. The Cheetah Girls franchise was notably successful in merchandise and sales, with its 2003 debut film premiering to over 84 million global viewers and its sequel to 8.1 million American viewers, becoming the most successful film in the series; an 86-date concert tour featuring the group was ranked among the top 10 concert tours of 2006, selling out with 73,500 tickets in three minutes at one point. Disney Channel holds rights to theatrically released feature films, some shared with sister network Freeform, including films from Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures (such as Walt Disney Pictures, Walt Disney Animation Studios, and Pixar), and also features films from Bagdasarian Productions like The Chipmunk Adventure and Alvin and the Chipmunks Meet Frankenstein, though most are not currently owned by Disney. Between programming and ads, the channel features bumpers, with the creator of the four-note mnemonic introduced in 2002 being Alex Lasarenko, identified by the YouTube documentary channel Defunctland in 2022. ESPN's broadcasts of the Little League World Series have included cross-promotions with music-related Disney Channel properties such as High School Musical, the Jonas Brothers, Camp Rock, and Phineas and Ferb. In March 2023, Disney Channel broadcast a live professional sporting event for the first time, airing a youth-oriented alternate broadcast of an NHL game—the Big City Greens Classic—as part of ESPN's coverage, themed around the animated series Big City Greens and visualizing player and puck data with 3D animated players. Disney Jr. is a daily morning program block for preschoolers, succeeding Playhouse Disney, which launched on April 6, 1997, as part of Disney Channel's morning lineup. On May 26, 2010, Disney General Entertainment Content (then Disney-ABC Television Group) announced the expansion of the block into a 24/7 cable and satellite channel that debuted on March 23, 2012. The channel is commercial-free and competes with other preschool-focused channels like Nick Jr. and Universal Kids (formerly PBS Kids Sprout and Sprout). It features programming from Disney Channel's preschool library and films from the Walt Disney Pictures film library. On its launch, Disney Junior took over the channel space previously held by Soapnet, a Disney-owned network for soap operas, due to the decline of that genre and the rise of on-demand and digital viewing. Soapnet ceased operations on December 31, 2013. The Playhouse Disney block on Disney Channel rebranded as Disney Junior on February 14, 2011, and international channels followed; the names were shortened to "Disney Jr." on June 1, 2024, though pronounced the same. Disney-ABC Television Group had planned to launch a Playhouse Disney-branded channel in the U.S. in 2001 but never did, despite launching it internationally. Disney XD, launched on February 13, 2009, as the successor to Toon Disney, targets young audiences aged 6 to 14, including girls, and features action and comedy programming from Disney Channel and the former Jetix block, along with original and syndicated shows. Unlike Disney Channel and Disney Junior, Disney XD operates as an ad-supported service, similar to Toon Disney. The "XD" in its name has no official meaning, despite being associated with a former Disney.com mini-site called Disney Xtreme Digital. Disney Channel Animation, also known as "Disney Channel Animation," is the television animation production studio division of Walt Disney Studios based in Glendale, California, producing original animated programming for the three main Disney-branded television channels. A live-action production studio based in Studio City, Los Angeles, provides original sitcoms and comedy programs primarily for Disney Channel, with many projects co-produced and financed by the Walt Disney Company. Walt Disney EMEA Productions Limited, located in London, England, co-produces original programs in Europe with other companies. Disney Original Documentary is a banner from Disney Branded Television for documentary programs broadcast on Disney Channel and released on Disney+, launched on December 9, 2021. In 2010, Disney Channel All Star Party was released for the Nintendo Wii, a four-player mascot party game with stages resembling board games featuring characters from shows like Sonny with a Chance, Wizards of Waverly Place, and JONAS L.A. Several video games based on the Phineas and Ferb series were released by Disney Interactive Studios, and the Disney Channel website included Flash games with characters from franchises such as Kim Possible and Hannah Montana. In June 2012, the Walt Disney Company announced it would stop advertising or promoting food or beverage products that do not meet strict nutritional guidelines, making Disney Channel the first media company to take such a stance on junk food marketing to children; advertising appears only as underwriter sponsorships during promotional breaks. On July 1, 2012, Disney Channel began providing Descriptive Video Service audio in compliance with the 21st Century Communications and Video Accessibility Act of 2010, offering audio descriptions for the blind in the 25 largest markets and on the five highest-rated cable and satellite channels, including Disney Channel. This is indicated by an on-screen mark and a 2-tone sound repeated three times at the start of episodes of Gravity Falls, Austin & Ally, Good Luck Charlie, and Phineas and Ferb, and on newer episodes of Little Einsteins on Disney Junior (with ABC placing the mark in the bottom-left corner). Disney Channel has a presence in various regions across the Americas, most of Europe, the Middle East, Africa, India, and Japan, with former channel versions available or used in Australia, New Zealand, Italy, the United Kingdom and Ireland, Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, Turkey, Spain, and Brazil, though most ceased broadcasting in the early 2020s, with content moving to Disney+ or Disney+ Hotstar. On December 14, 2022, Disney ceased distributing programs in Russia in response to the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine. The channel licenses its programming to certain broadcast and cable channels outside the U.S. (including formerly Family Channel in Canada), regardless of whether a localized feed exists. Some critics have disapproved of Disney Channel's marketing strategy led by Anne Sweeney, president from 1996 to 2014, who focused programming on preteen and teenage girls and reduced animated content. In 2002, nearly all Walt-era and pre-1990s programming was removed from the channel, including the late-night "Vault Disney" block, which previously dominated the schedule since 1983. In 2008, Sweeney stated that Disney Channel, through its multi-platform marketing using television and music, would become "the major profit driver" for the Walt Disney Company. The channel has also pulled or re-shot episodes due to content deemed inappropriate for its audience, either for humor or due to real-life events.

Doab (English: /ˈdoʊɑːb/) is a term used in South Asia for the tract of land lying between two confluent rivers and is similar to an interfluve. According to the Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary, R. S. McGregor notes its Persian origin, defining it as do-āb (دوآب, literally "two [bodies of] water") as a region lying between and reaching to the confluence of two rivers. In North India and Pakistan, where numerous Himalayan rivers divide the plains into doabs, the Indo-Gangetic plains consist of alternating regions of river, khadir, and bangar. Areas near rivers are low-lying floodplains, typically fertile khadir, while higher-lying areas away from rivers are bangar, less prone to flooding but generally less fertile. Khadir is also known as nali or naili, especially in northern Haryana, where it refers to the fertile prairie tract between the Ghaggar river and the southern limits of the Saraswati channel depression, which floods during rains. Within the bangar area, barani refers to low-rain areas where rain-fed dry farming is practiced, now often dependent on tubewells for irrigation; the Bagar tract, a dry sandy region on the border of Rajasthan adjoining Haryana and Punjab, is an example of barani land. Nahri refers to canal-irrigated land, such as the Rangoi tract, which is irrigated by the Rangoi channel/canal built to carry floodwaters from the Ghaggar river to dry areas. Historically, villages in the doabs have been officially classified as khadir, khadir-bangar (mixed), or bangar for centuries, with agricultural tax rates based on a tiered land-productivity scale. The Doab specifically designates the flat alluvial tract between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers, extending from the Sivalik Hills to their confluence at Prayagraj, also known as the Ganges-Yamuna Doab or Ganga Doab. This region covers about 23,360 square miles (60,500 square km), measuring approximately 500 miles (805 km) in length and 60 miles (97 km) in width. During the British Raj, the Doab was divided into three administrative districts: Upper Doab (Meerut), Middle Doab (Agra), and Lower Doab (Allahabad). Currently, the Doab includes the following states and districts: Dehradun and Haridwar; Saharanpur, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Baghpat, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Gautam Buddh Nagar, and Bulandshahr; Etah, Kasganj, Aligarh, Agra, Hathras, Firozabad, Mainpuri, and Mathura in the trans-Yamuna Braj region; and Farrukhabad, Kannauj, Etawah, Auraiya, Kanpur (Urban & Rural), Fatehpur, Kaushambi, and Allahabad. In the Punjab region of Pakistan and India, each doab has a distinct name, said to have been coined by Raja Todar Mal, a minister of Mughal emperor Akbar. These names (except "Indus Sagar") are formed by combining the first letters in the Persian alphabet of the rivers that bound the doab, from east to west. For example, "Chaj" (چج) = Chanāb (چناب) + Jehlam (جہلم). The Sind Sagar Doab lies between the Indus and Jhelum rivers; the Chaj Doab lies between the Jhelum and Chenab rivers; the Rachna Doab (a considerable portion of which is Majha) lies between the Chenab and Ravi rivers; the Bari Doab (a considerable portion of which is Majha) lies between the Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej rivers; the Bist Doab (or Doaba) lies between the Beas and Sutlej rivers; and the Raichur Doab, a triangular region in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka between the Krishna River and its tributary the Tungabhadra River, is named after the town of Raichur.

"Doki Doki Morning" is a song by the Japanese heavy metal band Babymetal, released in Japan as an independent DVD single on October 22, 2011, and serves as the first single from their debut album Babymetal. The song introduced all three members to heavy metal music; Nakamoto noted she had never heard such musical heaviness before, while Mizuno initially preferred dancing over singing. During production, the signature Kitsune hand gesture (similar to the sign of the horns) was developed. Vocals for the song were recorded on October 30, 2010. It first appeared in the Sakura Gakuin album Sakura Gakuin 2010 Nendo: Message, released on April 27, 2011, as part of the Jūonbu ("heavy music club") sub-unit. A limited-edition DVD single was announced on October 12, 2011, and later released as a standard digital download on October 22 and 23, 2011, available for pre-sale at the Sakura Gakuin Festival 2011 held at Mt. Rainier Hall "Shibuya Pleasure Pleasure," and subsequently sold in limited quantities on ASmart, Amazon, Tower Records Online, and Tower Records Shinjuku starting October 24. The limited edition included a DVD with the "Doki Doki ☆ Morning" music video and a cut focusing on the choreography for live performances, along with a towel embossed with either the band's logo or the Juonbu Records label. A CD single was released on April 6, 2012, packaged with a T-shirt. The song was later released as a promotional single in the United Kingdom on December 13, 2015. The track features a "modern heaviness" sound with dark, atmospheric instrumentals that transition into a catchier, brighter melody, including lyrics such as "Rin rin rin! Ohayō, wake up" (Ring ring ring! Good morning, wake up). Kikuchi highlighted that the tone contrasted directly with Japanese kei-on music (light music), leading the band to form under the Jūonbu label to signify this difference. Nakamoto, whose vocals were recorded separately from Mizuno and Kikuchi, needed to speak quickly and clearly in the verses. The song peaked at number 80 on the Billboard Japan Top Independent Albums and Singles chart for the week dated November 7, 2011. Directed by Shimon Tanaka, the music video shooting was completed by October 2011; Nakamoto mentioned that Tanaka wanted to appear in it but found the choreography difficult. The abridged version of the video was released on the Toy's Factory YouTube channel on October 12, 2011, with the full version posted on the official Babymetal channel on November 8, 2012. Metal Injection ranked the music video at number nine on "The Top 15 Metal Viral Videos of the Year" on December 8, 2011. The song premiered at the Sakura Gakuin Festival 2010 concert at Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse No. 1 on November 28, 2010. Su-metal recalled that during the interlude of the first performance, the group pretended to fall to the ground, fearing embarrassment, but the audience's positive reaction made her feel happy and affirmed her identity as Su-metal and Babymetal. On March 4, 2012, fellow Sakura Gakuin members Marina Horiuchi, Ayaka Miyoshi, and Airi Matsui covered the song as a "Shuffle Unit" during the Sakura Gakuin concert Sakura Gakuin Hōkago Anthology at the Nihonbashi Mitsui Hall. On December 8, 2013, Hana Taguchi, Saki Ooga, and Aiko Yamaide covered it as another "Shuffle Unit" at the Sakura Gakuin 3rd Anniversary: Live at the Amuse Musical Theater. Kiba of Akiba covered the song on the joint single "Babymetal × Kiba of Akiba." Credits are adapted from the album liner notes of Sakura Gakuin 2010 Nendo: Message and Babymetal.

Dolly, a female Finn-Dorset sheep born on 5 July 1996 and died on 14 February 2003, was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell. She was created at the Roslin Institute in Scotland by Keith Campbell, Ian Wilmut, and colleagues from the University of Edinburgh and PPL Therapeutics, using a technique called somatic cell nuclear transfer, where a nucleus from a mammary gland cell was transferred into an unfertilized egg cell that had its nucleus removed. The resulting hybrid cell was stimulated to divide and, when it developed into a blastocyst, was implanted into a surrogate mother. Dolly was the first clone produced from a cell taken from an adult mammal, proving that genes in a mature, differentiated somatic cell can revert to an embryonic totipotent state and develop into a whole organism. Although not the first animal ever cloned—John Gurdon had previously used adult somatic cells to clone African clawed frogs in 1958—Dolly gained widespread media attention as the first such clone from an adult mammal. She lived at the Roslin Institute throughout her life, where she was bred with a Welsh Mountain ram and produced six lambs: Bonnie in April 1998, twins Sally and Rosie in 1999, and triplets Lucy, Darcy, and Cotton in 2000. In 2001, at age four, she developed arthritis, which was treated with anti-inflammatory drugs, and by 2003, she had a progressive lung disease, specifically ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (Jaagsiekte), caused by the retrovirus JSRV. No link between her cloning and the disease was found, as similar cases occurred in other sheep in the flock. Dolly was euthanized at six years old, which is shorter than the typical 11–12-year lifespan of a Finn Dorset, though her telomeres were found to be short, leading some to speculate she had a genetic age of six. However, Roslin scientists found no evidence of advanced aging or health defects from cloning. After her death, her body was preserved via taxidermy and displayed at the National Museum of Scotland. In 2016, a study of 13 cloned sheep, including four from the same cell line as Dolly, found no long-term health issues beyond minor osteoarthritis, concluding there was no detrimental effect of cloning on aged offspring. Following Dolly’s success, many large mammals were cloned, including pigs, deer, horses, and bulls, though some attempts, like cloning argali, failed. Cloning efficiency was initially very low—Dolly was the only adult lamb from 277 attempts—and Wilmut later stated nuclear transfer may never be efficient for human use. By 2014, Chinese scientists achieved 70–80% success rates in cloning pigs, and by 2016, Sooam Biotech was producing 500 cloned embryos daily, while commercial pet cloning services like Viagen charged $50,000 for a dog, $30,000 for a cat, and $85,000 for a horse. Cloning has potential applications in preserving endangered species and reviving extinct ones; in 2009, scientists cloned the Pyrenean ibex, the first extinct animal to be cloned, though the newborn died shortly after birth due to lung defects. In 2016, four clones of Dolly—Daisy, Debbie, Dianna, and Denise—were alive and healthy at nine years old, and were later euthanized in 2017 after research showed they were aging normally. Scientific American noted that Dolly’s main legacy was in advancing stem cell research, including the discovery of induced pluripotent stem cells. In 2000, researchers cloned a lamb named Diana with a human gene for alpha 1-antitrypsin, which was activated in her mammary gland to produce therapeutic milk. In 2018, Chinese scientists created the first cloned primates, Zhong Zhong and Hua Hua, using the same method as Dolly. In 2019, five gene-edited cloned monkeys were created using CRISPR-Cas9, intended for medical research. In 2003, Belgian artist Dominique Goblet published a comic strip titled “2004 Apparition de Dolly dans la campagne anglaise” about her.

Dollywood is a theme park jointly owned by Herschend and Dolly Parton through her entertainment company, Dolly Parton Productions, and is located in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, within the Knoxville metropolitan area near the gateway to The Great Smoky Mountains. It hosts nearly 3 million guests annually from mid-March to the Christmas holidays and is the largest ticketed tourist attraction in Tennessee, having won several international awards. In addition to thrill rides, the park features traditional Smoky Mountain crafts, food, and music, hosting concerts and musical events each year, including performances by Dolly Parton and her family as well as national and local acts. The park is part of a 150-acre (61 ha) Dollywood amusement destination that includes the 35-acre (14 ha) Dollywood's Splash Country water park, the 20-acre (8.1 ha) Dollywood's DreamMore Resort and Spa, and the 5-acre (2.0 ha) Dolly Parton's Stampede Dinner Attraction. Originally opened on June 10, 1961, as "Rebel Railroad" by the Robbins brothers from Blowing Rock, North Carolina, the park was themed around the centennial of the Civil War, featuring a steam train, general store, blacksmith shop, and saloon, with riders protected by Confederates from attacks by Union soldiers, train robbers, and Native Americans. It was modeled after their earlier park, Tweetsie Railroad. In 1964, it was renamed "Goldrush Junction" with a wild west theme similar to Tweetsie Railroad. In 1970, Art Modell, owner of the Cleveland Browns, purchased the park and added an outdoor theater and the Robert F. Thomas Chapel. In 1975, the name changed to "Goldrush," and in 1976, Jack and Pete Herschend, owners of Silver Dollar City, bought the park, which continued operating as Goldrush that year. In 1977, the Herschends renamed it "Silver Dollar City Tennessee" to make it a sister park to their original Silver Dollar City in Branson, Missouri, spending about $1 million on upgrades and adding two new steam locomotives, #70 and #71, and the remains of engine #72 from the White Pass & Yukon Route Railroad. In 1986, Dolly Parton, who grew up in the area, acquired an interest in the park and it reopened on May 3, 1986, as "Dollywood." Parton stated she became involved to bring jobs to her home region after achieving success in her career. The park employs approximately 4,000 people, making it the largest employer in the community. From 1986 to 2010, the park doubled in size to 150 acres (61 ha). On November 16, 2010, Dollywood earned the Liseberg Applause Award, which Dolly Parton accepted at the IAAPA Attractions Expo 2010 in Orlando. The 1986 reopening included the Rivertown Junction area with Smoky Mountain River Rampage, Back Porch Theater, Aunt Granny's Dixie Fixins' Restaurant, Dolly's Tennessee Mountain Home, and "Rags to Riches: The Dolly Parton Story" museum; the "The Butter Churn" ride was removed, and attendance doubled to over a million guests. In 1987, the Daydream Ridge area opened with the Mountain Slidewinder, Mountain Dan's Burger House, Sweet Dreams Candy Shop, The Rainbow Factory, and Critter Creek Playground; engine #70 was restored. In 1988, the 1,739-seat Celebrity Theater opened with the "Showcase of Stars" concert series. Five new children's rides were added to Fun Country, including a Zamperla Balloon Race. The Dollywood Foundation was established to provide books and school supplies to children in Sevier County. In 1989, Thunder Express, a steel mine train coaster, was built adjacent to Blazing Fury and relocated from Six Flags Over Mid-America; the 1989 season was the last for the National Mountain Music Festival. In 1990, a 1924 Dentzel Carousel was relocated to near the train depot, replacing the Silver Dollar Saloon; a 600-seat Gaslight Theater opened nearby. The Smoky Mountain Christmas Festival premiered in November, extending the operating season into December. In 1991, Eagle Mountain Sanctuary, an outdoor aviary, and the Wings of America Theater with the Birds of Prey show and the 300-seat Valley Theater were added. In 1992, the Showstreet area opened with the Showstreet Palace Theater, The Butterfly Emporium, The Backstage Restaurant, The Spotlight Bakery, Friendship Gardens, and WDLY-FM, a working radio station; the main entrance moved from Rivertown Junction to Showstreet; the Barnwood Theater became Imagination Station. Attendance topped 2 million for the first time in 1992. In 1993, Fun Country was renovated into The Country Fair with the Wonder Wheel (60 ft tall), Twist and Shout, and Tennessee Twister; the Balloon Race ride was relocated to Daydream Ridge. "Sunset Musicfest" debuted in 1994; the Gaslight Theater became the Heartsong Theater. In 1995, the Jukebox Junction 1950s "Main Street" area opened with Rockin' Roadway, The Pines Theater, Red's Diner, and Cas Walker's Music Store; Sunset Musicfest did not return. In 1996, the Dollywood Boulevard area opened with Thunder Road, Silver Screen Café, and Centerstage gift shop. In 1997, "U Pick Nick" aired in the Celebrity Theater; the Flooded Mine dark ride was closed and demolished in October; Silver Screen Café became DJ Platters. In 1998, Daredevil Falls, billed as "The Highest and Fastest Waterfall Ride in America" with a 62 ft (19 m) drop, opened in the former Flooded Mine location. Thunder Express was closed in September and sold to Magic Springs Theme Park in Arkansas; the antique carousel was removed and replaced with a new Chance Rides carousel. In 1999, the Tennessee Tornado steel looping coaster opened in the former Thunder Express area; the Southern Gospel Museum and Hall of Fame opened; the Balloon Race ride was removed. In 2000, Daydream Ridge was renovated into Dreamland Forest, a children's mountain-themed interactive play area. The Festival of Nations premiered in April 2001. In 2001, Dolly's Splash Country, a 25-acre (100,000 m²) water park, opened adjacent to Dollywood's parking lot. In 2002, Dollywood Boulevard was redeveloped into Adventures in Imagination; Smoky Mountain Wilderness Adventure replaced Thunder Road; a new Dolly museum, Chasing Rainbows, opened in the former DJ Platters building. In 2003, KidsFest premiered and Imagination Station became Celebration Hall; the "Showcase of Stars" concert series ended. In 2004, Thunderhead Gap opened with the Thunderhead wooden roller coaster; the Country Fair Falls log flume was demolished in November; most Country Fair rides, including the Swingamajig, Tennessee Twister, The Convoy, and The Barnstormer, were removed to make room for new rides in 2005, which included Dizzy Disk, Amazing Flying Elephants, Lemon Twist, Shooting Star, Sky Rider, VeggieTales Sideshow Spin, Waltzing Swinger, Piggy Parade, Busy Bees, and Lucky Ducky; the National Southern Gospel & Harvest Celebration debuted. In 2006, the Timber Tower ride, along with Lil' Loggers Landing, Beaver Creek, Beaver Creek Boat Float, and Lumberjack Lifts, opened in a new area adjacent to Thunderhead; the Barbeque & Bluegrass festival premiered. In 2007, Mystery Mine, a Gerstlauer Eurofighter coaster with two vertical lift hills, dark ride elements, fire effects, a 95-degree 85-foot (26 m) drop, a heartline roll, and a dive loop, opened using an abandoned mine shaft theme; the ride cost $17 million ($25.8 million in 2024 dollars). In 2008, River Battle, an interactive water raft ride, opened in Wilderness Pass, connecting Timber Canyon and Craftsman's Valley; "Thunder Road" returned to Imagination Cinema; Della's Lye Soap shop moved to Wilderness Pass; a new exhibit for the Wings of America show birds was relocated; the Polar Express 4-D Experience was shown during Smoky Mountain Christmas. In 2009, new shows "Imaginé" by Le Grand Cirque and "Sha-Kon-O-Hey! Land of Blue Smoke," featuring music by Dolly Parton and the story of the last family in the Smoky Mountains, were introduced; "Imaginé" headlined Festival of Nations; "Thunder Road" was renamed "White Lightning" and then replaced by Journey to the Center of the Earth: 4-D Adventure; a multi-line zipline attraction, SkyZip (owned by Skyline Eco-Adventures of Maui, Hawaii), opened as the first multi-line zip line tour in a theme park. In 2010, Adventure Mountain opened in Wilderness Pass at a cost of $5 million, featuring three adventure courses—Geyser Gorge, Black Bear Cliff, and Rocky Top—with 100 rope features, swinging beams, suspension bridges, flying islands, and floating stairs, ranging from a few inches to over 26 feet (7.9 m) in height; it included a scaled-down play area, Camp Teachittoomee; the park also brought back "Sha-Kon-O-Hey! Land of Blue Smoke" and changed its logo for its 25th anniversary. In 2011, Owens Farm with a $5.5 million giant swing, Barnstormer, replaced Dreamland Forest; the area included a play area for younger guests; Christmas on Ice, a new ice skating show, premiered in DP's Celebrity Theater and headlined Smoky Mountain Christmas. Wild Eagle opened on March 24, 2012, as the first Bolliger & Mabillard Wing Coaster in the United States and was the biggest investment in Dollywood history; in 2012, the operator of SkyZip sued Dollywood, blaming it for damaging the zip line network during construction of Wild Eagle, though Dollywood blamed storms; the two settled out of court, and Dollywood took over SkyZip operations, closing it in 2019; Timber Tower was dismantled before opening in 2012 due to a lawsuit with the manufacturer; the VeggieTales name was removed from Sideshow Spin in 2012; Adventure Mountain was permanently closed after the 2012 season. In 2013, Dollywood focused on family time, introducing Cirque Shanghai, Mystic India, One World Party, over 50 new international food items, "Great American Summer" (replacing KidsFest), including the Great American Country Show, Gazillion Bubbles, The Little Engine Playhouse, and Salute to America, extended hours, and a nightly fireworks show; Smoky Mountain Christmas added a show based on Dolly Parton's version of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol; the slogan was "Make Time for Happy!" and Imagination Cinema became Dreamsong Theater, playing Dolly's My People. In 2014, FireChaser Express, a dual-launch family coaster, replaced Adventure Mountain in Wilderness Pass; the slogan changed to "Love Every Moment"; Smoky Mountain Christmas added a Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer meet-and-greet, Holly Jolly Junction. Dollywood's DreamMore Resort and Spa opened adjacent to Dollywood's Splash Country in 2015. For its 30th anniversary, the park redesigned the resort entrance and added two new Festival of Nations shows, "Rhythm of the Dance" and "Timber"; Cas Walker's was demolished; six new shows were added to "Great American Summer"; the Showcase of Stars concert series was revived; Rock the Smokies, a Christian music festival, debuted; Rudolph and friends returned to Smoky Mountain Christmas. In 2010, Parton expressed interest in expanding Dollywood with new parks and a resort, stating they may eventually open in other parts of the country to reflect local culture. On August 21, 2013, Parton announced Dollywood's DreamMore Resort and Spa, which opened on July 27, 2015. On June 13, 2016, Lightning Rod, a Rocky Mountain Construction wooden coaster, opened as the world's first launched wooden coaster and the fastest wooden coaster in the world. In 2017, a 200-foot (61 m) freefall ride, Drop Line, opened to replace Timber Tower, along with a junior roller coaster, Whistle Punk Chaser; two new seasonal events debuted; Dollywood's Splash Country added the TailSpin Racer mat racer slide complex; Sideshow Spin and River Battle were removed. In 2018, the former River Battle site became the Plaza at Wilderness Pass, a covered open space for relaxation and seasonal events; the Spring Mix music series and the 2018 "Season of Showstoppers" marked the park's largest investment in entertainment; the Festival of Nations featured three new headliners: Flamenco Kings starring Los Vivancos (Pines Theater), National Dance Company of Siberia (Celebrity Theater), and Ladysmith Black Mambazo (Showstreet Palace Theater); the first Summer Celebration included DRUMLine Live! in Celebrity Theater.

Dollywood is organized into 11 themed areas—Showstreet, Rivertown Junction, Craftsman's Valley, The Village, Country Fair, Timber Canyon, Wilderness Pass, Jukebox Junction, Owens Farm, Adventures in Imagination, and Wildwood Grove—reflecting the historical eras and culture of East Tennessee, with Owens Farm and Adventures in Imagination exploring Dolly Parton's life and imagination. Many attractions focus on the history and culture of the Southern Appalachian region. The park features a variety of attractions, including Showstreet Palace Theater and Celebrity Theater, Dolly's Tennessee Mountain Home, Back Porch Theater, Smoky Mountain River Rampage, Dollywood Grist Mill, Valley Theater, Eagle Mountain Sanctuary, Wings of America Theater, Robert F. Thomas Chapel, Calico Falls Schoolhouse, Tennessee Tornado, Blazing Fury, Daredevil Falls, craft exhibits, the 3 ft (914 mm) narrow gauge Dollywood Express steam train, Imagination Playhouse, Village Carousel, The Amazing Flying Elephants, Lemon Twist, Shooting Star, Sky Rider, The Waltzing Swinger, Piggy Parade, Busy Bees, Lucky Ducky, Dolly's Demolition Derby, The Scrambler, Mystery Mine, Thunderhead, Drop Line, Whistle Punk Chaser, Lumberjack Lifts, Rockin' Roadway, Pines Theater, Lightning Rod, Barnstormer, Behind the Seams and Song-teller Museums, The Plaza at Wilderness Pass, Wild Eagle—America's first winged coaster—and FireChaser Express, a dual-launch coaster. In 2017, a 200-foot (61 m) freefall ride called Drop Line, which replaced Timber Tower, opened along with a junior roller coaster called Whistle Punk Chaser. Two new seasonal events debuted, and Dollywood's Splash Country added the TailSpin Racer mat racer slide complex. Sideshow Spin and River Battle were removed. In 2018, the former River Battle site was transformed into the Plaza at Wilderness Pass, a new open space with covered seating for relaxing and enjoying seasonal events. The 2018 "Season of Showstoppers" marked the park's largest investment in entertainment in its history, featuring headliners including Flamenco Kings starring Los Vivancos (Pines Theater), National Dance Company of Siberia (Celebrity Theater), and Ladysmith Black Mambazo (Showstreet Palace Theater). The first Summer Celebration included DRUMLine Live! in Celebrity Theater, which highlights musical styles from Historically Black Colleges and Universities using video screens and special effects to enhance soul, R&B, country, and other music. Renovations included upgrades to Aunt Granny's and rebranding and renaming of two shops. Work began in October 2017 on "Wildwood Grove," adding eleven new experiences, including a suspended family coaster (Dragonflier), a restaurant (Till & Harvest), an indoor play area (Hidden Hollow), an outdoor splash pad (Wildwood Creek), a swinging boat ride (The Great Tree Swing), and a 50 ft tall tree with a butterfly canopy (The Wildwood Tree). The $37 million, 5-acre development, described as "a land built from Dolly Parton's dreams," opened on May 10, 2019, as part of a $300 million 6-year expansion project. In October 2019, Dollywood announced its first new festival in 14 years, Dollywood's Flower & Food Festival, featuring 10 to 15 foot tall topiaries based on Dolly's songs like "Coat of Many Colors," photo opportunities, a rainbow sky over Showstreet, and food. The festival was originally scheduled for May 8 to June 14, 2020, but was deferred to May 7 to June 13, 2021. In October 2019, Dollywood filed plans for a new resort adjacent to Splash Country and DreamMore Resort, featuring a 310-room hotel, a 325-seat restaurant, and a conference space, creating 100 jobs. In June 2021, Dollywood announced a $500 million expansion, including details about the HeartSong Lodge & Resort, which will have 302 rooms, five floors of suites, a four-story atrium with a large central fireplace, and multiple shopping and culinary experiences. HeartSong Lodge is scheduled to open in 2023, along with campgrounds, three additional resorts, and a "record-breaking" attraction. During the 2022 off-season, the Silver Dollar Mine tunnel connecting the lower section of Craftsman's Valley and The Village was removed, creating more open space for guests to walk through and enjoy views of the Dollywood Express. The parking complex was renovated to better utilize lots at both Dollywood and Splash Country, with guest traffic lanes swapped for tram lanes, eliminating previous intersections and introducing a one-way circuit that removes the old two-way traffic pattern. Two extra parking toll booths (four attendants) and additional staging lanes were added to reduce wait times. Other improvements included renovations to Iron Horse Pizza (formerly Victoria's Pizza) for greater production capacity and seating, a complete makeover of the Emporium for a modern shopping experience, and the removal of two buildings—the former Eagle Shop and the former Christmas Cottage—to provide wider walkways. On August 5, 2022, it was announced that Big Bear Mountain, a new roller coaster under construction, opened on May 12, 2023, and is the longest in the park's history. In 2019, Dollywood won Golden Ticket awards for Best Kids' Area, Best Guest Experience, and Best Christmas Event of 2018. In 2019, Coaster101.com named Lightning Rod "Wooden Roller Coaster of the Decade." In 2021, Dollywood's Smoky Mountain Christmas won the Golden Ticket Award for Best Christmas Event for the 13th straight year. In June 2022, Tripadvisor named Dollywood the number one theme park in the U.S. Dollywood received the Applause Award in 2010 from Liseberg in Gothenburg, Sweden, recognizing its management, operations, and creative accomplishments. In 2017, Dollywood won Golden Ticket awards for Friendliest Park, Best Christmas Event, Best Food, and Best Show. In 2018, Dollywood received a Golden Ticket award in the Best Food category, marking its fourth win in seven years, and also won Golden Tickets for Best Shows, Friendliest Park, and Best Christmas Event, and was ranked third best park in the world. In the 2018 USA Today 10Best Readers' Choice Awards, Dollywood was ranked sixth best amusement park in the U.S., DreamMore Resort and Spa was ranked first in Best Amusement Park Hotel, and Aunt Granny's Restaurant was ranked first in Best Amusement Park Restaurant. Dreamland Drive-In was ranked third in Best Amusement Park Entertainment, and Dollywood's Splash Country was ranked sixth in Best Outdoor Water Park.

Dolores María Fonzi (born 19 July 1978) is an Argentine television, theatre, and film actress. Several of her films have received critical acclaim, including Burnt Money (2000), Waiting for the Messiah (2000), Bottom of the Sea (2003), The Aura (2005), and Paulina (2015). In 2023, she made her directorial debut with the comedy-drama Blondi.[1] Her second film, the legal drama Belén, is competing for the Golden Shell at the 73rd San Sebastian International Film Festival.[2] She was born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and after her parents' separation, her mother, María del Rosario Cárrega, returned with her children to Adrogué, where Dolores and her brothers Tomás and Diego grew up. She studied acting at the school of Carlos Gandolfo; her brother Tomás Fonzi is also an actor in Argentina.[3][4] In 1996, at seventeen years old, she made her first television appearance in the series La nena. In 1998, Cris Morena chose her to play Clara Vázquez in Verano del '98, alongside her brother, who played Benjamín Vázquez. Thanks to the series' success and her portrayal as a villain, she gained significant popularity and success. At the end of 1999, she left Verano del '98 to join Marcelo Piñeyro's film Burnt Money, marking her film debut in a role as a sex worker.[5] She also appeared in Waiting for the Messiah. In 2001, she gained recognition by joining the cast of El sodero de mi vida on Canal 13, where she played a girl with a slight mental retardation. She experimented with Luis Ortega on the tape Caja negra, where she acted and participated in the integral creation. She later appeared in films such as Private Lives, Bottom of the Sea, The Aura, La mujer rota, Salamandra, El club de la muerte, and El campo, for which she was nominated for the Silver Condor Awards for Best Actress. In 2003, she starred in the unitary series Disputas and in the adaptation of John Ford's play Lástima que sea una puta. The following year, she starred with Mariano Martínez in the terror unit Sangre fría on Telefe. From 2006 to 2014, she starred and produced the miniseries Soy tu fan, which was adapted by Canana Films in Mexico in 2010. She also starred in the series El tiempo no para on Canal 9. From 2005 to 2008, she participated in three chapters of Mujeres asesinas. Her return to television was in 2012 with her role in Graduados, a new Underground production for Telefe. She also participated in the TV Pública series En terapia with actors Norma Aleandro, Diego Peretti, Leonardo Sbaraglia, Ailín Salas, Julieta Cardinali, and Germán Palacios. She resumed her theater career as the protagonist of the play Isósceles. That year, she also filmed El Crítico by Hernán Guerschuny, a co-production between HC Films and Lagarto Cine, where she had the lead alongside Rafael Spregelburd. On television, she appeared as a guest actress in two episodes of the series Aliados. In 2015, she starred in the film Paulina, a remake of the 1960 film starring Mirtha Legrand. The film achieved strong box office performance and favorable reviews, being praised at the Cannes Festival. For her performance, she was awarded the Havana Star Prize for Best Actress at the 17th Havana Film Festival New York.[6] She also acted in the film Truman starring Ricardo Darín. In 2016, she joined the cast of the series La Leona, playing Eugenia Leone. From 2008 to 2014, she was in a relationship with actor Gael García Bernal,[7] whom she met on the set of the 2001 film Private Lives.[8] They had two children, born in 2009 and 2011.[7] Afterward, she entered a relationship with filmmaker Santiago Mitre, whom she met during the filming of Paulina in 2014.[9]

Donald Clarence Simpson (October 29, 1943 – January 19, 1996) was an American film producer, screenwriter, and actor renowned for his work on major blockbuster films of the 1980s and 1990s. He began his career in the 1970s at Warner Bros. and Paramount Pictures, where he worked in marketing exploitation films, including Woodstock and A Clockwork Orange, and co-wrote and had a small role in the 1976 film Cannonball. In 1975, he was interviewed for a position at Paramount by his friend Steve Tisch, who declined the offer, and was later named vice-president of production in 1977 and president in 1981. He was fired in 1982 after passing out during a studio meeting due to drug use and was known for managing eight productions simultaneously and frequently throwing tantrums during filming. He formed a professional partnership with Jerry Bruckheimer, producing successful films such as Flashdance (1983), Beverly Hills Cop (1984), Top Gun (1986), Beverly Hills Cop II (1987), and The Rock (1996), the latter released posthumously. The duo earned Producers of the Year honors from the National Association of Theatre Owners in 1985 and 1988 and launched their own production company affiliated with Paramount in 1985. In 1990, they signed a five-year $300 million deal with Paramount, which ended after Days of Thunder (1990) underperformed at the box office despite a $60 million budget and grossing $158 million, with both parties blaming each other for the results. They later signed with Disney, with The Ref (1994) being a financial failure, but returned to success with Dangerous Minds, Crimson Tide, and Bad Boys in 1995. Simpson never married; he took Scientology classes in the 1970s but quit after spending $25,000 with no personal gains, and during Days of Thunder, he expelled Scientology leader David Miscavige after refusing to pay for a costly sound device. Known for his brash personality, Simpson made controversial remarks, such as criticizing Steven Spielberg and David Lynch, and claimed his primary duty as a producer was to make money. He worked out daily with equipment provided by Arnold Schwarzenegger and frequented Canyon Ranch for workouts and tanning. Though he claimed never to have had plastic surgery, reports indicate he underwent ten procedures between 1988 and 1994, including a penis-enlargement surgery, which led to infections and reversals. Simpson was infamous for his extravagant lifestyle, often describing making movies as the best thing after eating and having sex, and was a central figure in Hollywood's cocaine-party scene, hosting lavish all-night parties and being known for S&M preferences. He used cocaine since the 1970s, increasing his use over time, and was known for erratic behavior and excessive spending. In a 1994 interview, he claimed to have stopped using drugs and only had a food addiction, but screenwriter James Toback stated his drug use never ceased, prompting David Geffen and Jeffrey Katzenberg to intervene. Simpson refused traditional rehab and instead worked with doctor Stephen Ammerman, who developed a "dangerously unorthodox" detox program involving medications like morphine to manage withdrawal. Ammerman died in August 1995 at Simpson’s home from an accidental overdose of cocaine, Valium, venlafaxine, and morphine. Frustrated by Simpson’s drug use and declining performance, Bruckheimer ended their partnership in December 1995, agreeing to complete The Rock, which was dedicated to Simpson’s memory. Simpson died on January 19, 1996, in the bathroom of his Bel Air, Los Angeles, home, initially attributed to natural causes; an autopsy revealed he died of heart failure from combined drug intoxication, with 21 different drugs detected in his system, including antidepressants, stimulants, sedatives, and tranquilizers. Investigations revealed he obtained prescription drugs from 15 doctors, with 2,200 pills found in his bedroom closet, and his monthly prescription expenses totaled over $60,000. A 1998 book by Charles Fleming described him as "a supercharged simple-minded creature, an Aesop's fable on crystal meth." After his death, his brother Lary Simpson established a production banner to develop projects originated by Don Simpson, which continued until Lary’s death on January 25, 2023, at age 77. Simpson is credited as a producer on all films unless otherwise noted.

Donjuan Triumphant, a bay stallion foaled on 24 March 2013 in Ireland, is a Thoroughbred racehorse known for excelling in sprint distances. Bred by Patrick Cosgrove and the Dream Ahead Syndicate, he was consigned to the Goffs sale in November 2013 and purchased for €58,000 by Lynn Lodge Stud; he later returned as a yearling at the Tattersalls "breeze-up" sale in early 2015, where he was bought for 30,000 guineas by Middleham Park Racing. Trained by Richard Fahey at Malton, North Yorkshire, his name references the title character in the novel *The Phantom of the Opera*. He is a member of the first crop of foals sired by Dream Ahead, a sprinter with wins in the Prix Morny, Middle Park Stakes, July Cup, Haydock Sprint Cup, and Prix de la Forêt, and his progeny includes Glass Slippers, Dream of Dreams, and Al Wukair. His dam, Mathuna, won on her debut but failed to win in eight subsequent starts and was descended from Mariella, who won the Premio Roma, and is a half-sister to Sagaro. Donjuan Triumphant made his racecourse debut on 20 June 2015 at Redcar, finishing second by a head to Receding Waves, and sustained narrow defeats at Ayr, Carlisle, and Haydock before winning his first race at Ayr two weeks later by three and a quarter lengths with apprentice jockey Jack Garritty. He then won the Listed Rockingham Stakes at York on 10 October by one and a half lengths from Dhamaan and the Group 2 Critérium de Maisons-Laffitte in France on 11 October by five and a half lengths after taking the lead 200 metres from the finish. In 2016, he finished second to Quiet Reflection in the Temple Stakes and behind her in the Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot, and placed second to Signs of Blessing in the Group 1 Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville. He failed to win in the following races, including the Haydock Sprint Cup and the British Champions Sprint Stakes, and competed in minor races on synthetic tracks. In 2017, he was bought privately by Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha and transferred to Andrew Balding’s stable at Kingsclere, carrying King Power Racing’s blue and white colours. He won a minor race at Haydock in August 2017 after a lengthy absence, beating five opponents by one and a quarter lengths, and later ran in the Ayr Gold Cup, which was moved to Haydock due to waterlogging, winning by a short head. In 2018, he finished eighth in the British Champions Sprint Stakes at Ascot. On 10 November 2018, he won the Listed Wentworth Stakes at Doncaster on soft ground by a head, ridden by James Doyle and starting as a 2/1 favourite. After Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha’s death in the 2018 Leicester helicopter crash, Andrew Balding reflected on the tragedy and praised Donjuan Triumphant’s toughness and love for soft ground. In 2019, he made a strong comeback, finishing fourth in the Haydock Sprint Cup and third in the British Champions Sprint Stakes, and was rated 118 in the 2019 World's Best Racehorse Rankings, making him the 78th best racehorse globally. He retired at the end of 2019 and began his career as a breeding stallion at Haras de la Barbottiere in Sablé-sur-Sarthe in 2020 at a fee of €4,000.

Donald Andrew McClurkin Jr. (born November 9, 1959) is an American gospel singer and minister who has won three Grammy Awards, ten Stellar Awards, two BET Awards, two Soul Train Awards, one Dove Award, and one NAACP Image Award. He is one of the top-selling gospel artists, having sold over 13 million albums. Variety referred to him as a "Reigning King of Urban Gospel." McClurkin was born in Copiague, New York. At age eight, his two-year-old brother was killed by a speeding driver, causing family turmoil. He later experienced childhood sexual abuse from his great uncle and his great uncle's son. Two of his sisters struggled with substance abuse, prompting McClurkin to find solace in church and through an aunt who sang background vocals with gospel musician Andraé Crouch. By adolescence, he formed the McClurkin Singers and later the New York Restoration Choir, releasing recordings as early as 1975. He released three albums with the choir before launching a solo career. In 1989, he was hired as an associate minister at Marvin Winans' Perfecting Church in Detroit, Michigan, serving as an assistant for over a decade. In 1991, McClurkin was diagnosed with leukemia after experiencing sharp pain, swelling, and internal bleeding; at age 31, he chose to follow his own advice to "believe that God will save you" and practice what he preached. In 2001, he was ordained and sent by Marvin Winans to establish Perfecting Faith Church in Freeport, New York, where he serves as senior pastor. A friendship with a Warner Alliance executive led to his signing with the label for his 1996 self-titled album, produced by Bill Maxwell, Mark Kibble of Take 6, Cedric and Victor Caldwell, and Andraé Crouch. The album, featuring the popular song "Stand," went gold after being praised by Oprah Winfrey. At the 48th Annual Grammy Awards, he won Best Traditional Soul Gospel Album for "Psalms, Hymns & Spiritual Songs." McClurkin is best known for his hit songs "Stand" and "We Fall Down," which were played extensively on Gospel and Urban radio. His three solo albums have topped the Billboard Charts. Following the success of his near double platinum album "Live in London and More," he released "Psalms, Hymns and Spiritual Songs" in 2005 and "We All Are One: Live In Detroit" in 2009, both of which topped Billboard charts across genres. In 2014, he released "Duets," featuring artists such as Mary Mary’s Erica and Tina Campbell, Fred Hammond, John P. Kee, Dorinda Clark-Cole, Tramaine Hawkins, Israel Houghton, and Tye Tribbett. The album debuted at No. 45 on the Billboard 200 and No. 4 on the Gospel Billboard charts. His 2016 album "The Journey" debuted at number one on the Billboard Top Gospel Albums chart, marking his seventh solo release and including live performances of classics like "Speak to My Heart," "Great Is Your Mercy," "Stand," and "That’s What I Believe." His last recorded album, "A Different Song," was released in 2019 and debuted at No. 2 on the Gospel Billboard charts. McClurkin includes a language medley—Japanese, Russian, Spanish, and Dutch—in most live performances due to his love for sharing gospel music globally. Tom Versen and Tony Sisti of T&T Creative signed him to a radio syndication deal with Dial Global Local and syndicator Gary Bernstein, providing a mobile recording studio based in his church for on-the-road broadcasts. He stated, "As much as I love music and singing, I really love doing radio and the direct feedback I get from my listeners all over the country. I never thought I would be having this much fun doing radio, and I could touch and impact so many beautiful people." In 2009, he launched the television series *Perfecting Your Faith* on cable. His television appearances include *Good Morning America*, CBS’s *The Early Show*, *The View*, *Girlfriends*, and *The Parkers*. He has also appeared in films such as *The Gospel* and *The Fighting Temptations*, playing a single man or a church pastor. In 2002, McClurkin told a Christian website that due to sexual abuse and exposure to pornography, he had struggled with homosexuality, stating he "turned" gay as a result of childhood molestation and traumatic pornography exposure but was able to reverse his orientation through "will and prayer." He later said he had rejected that "lifestyle," asserting, "I’ve been through this and have experienced God’s power to change my lifestyle. I am delivered, and I know God can deliver others, too." His inclusion as a headlining performer for Senator Barack Obama’s 2008 presidential campaign sparked controversy due to his views on homosexuality, leading to his removal from the performance roster, though he still performed at one concert. In August 2013, he was disinvited from the 50th anniversary of the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom due to his ex-gay status being seen as disruptive. In 2015, he spoke out against same-sex marriage following the U.S. Supreme Court’s legalization of it nationwide. McClurkin has a son, Matthew, born in 2000. He is also related to singer Marsha McClurkin of the short-lived new jack swing group Abstrac. In 2018, McClurkin survived a serious road accident after losing consciousness while driving. In January 2026, McClurkin was sued for sexual assault by Giuseppe Corletto, a former personal assistant from 2004 to 2008. The lawsuit, filed in the Manhattan Supreme Court, claims Corletto met McClurkin in 2003 after reading his autobiography, which described his deliverance from homosexuality. Corletto became McClurkin’s assistant in 2004, and within two years, the lawsuit alleges McClurkin began grope him during "pray the gay away" sessions. The abuse is said to have occurred at Perfecting Faith Church and during work trips over several years. After an alleged assault in 2013, McClurkin allegedly wrote an email apologizing for his actions, referring to himself as a "dirty old man." McClurkin’s attorney responded that the allegations are "categorically false." The BET Awards are awarded annually by Black Entertainment Television; McClurkin has received two awards from five nominations. The Dove Awards are awarded annually by the Gospel Music Association; he has won four awards from thirteen nominations. The Grammy Awards are awarded annually by the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences; McClurkin has won three awards from five nominations. The Soul Train Music Awards are awarded annually; he has received two awards from five nominations. The Stellar Awards are awarded annually by SAGMA; McClurkin has received twelve awards from twenty-four nominations.

Doris Salcedo, born in 1958 in Bogotá, Colombia, is a visual artist and sculptor whose work is deeply rooted in her experiences of political violence and personal loss in Colombia. Her art uses common materials such as wooden furniture, clothing, concrete, grass, and rose petals to give form to pain, trauma, and the profound emptiness left by disappearance—experiences shaped by the disappearance of family members during Colombia’s civil conflict. Salcedo earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts from Jorge Tadeo Lozano University in 1980 and a Master of Fine Arts from New York University in 1984, after which she returned to Bogotá to teach at the Universidad Nacional de Colombia. She is married to Azriel Bibliowicz, a Colombian novelist and sociologist who studies the Jewish experience in Colombia, and they live and work in Bogotá. Her installations often address memory, forgetting, and the political dimensions of history. Works such as Unland: The Orphan's Tunic (1997) and the La Casa Viuda series from the early 1990s transform everyday objects like chairs and tables into memorials for victims of Colombia’s civil war. In Unland, a table made from two destroyed tables joined by a whitish veil of fabric—presumably an orphan’s tunic—contains hundreds of human hairs as thread, with Huyssen describing it as a “memory sculpture” where the table becomes a metaphor for the body of an orphaned community. Salcedo emphasizes that her art involves a process of metamorphosis, where materials charged with personal and historical meaning are reconfigured to evoke emotional and psychological resonance. In her 2002 work Noviembre 6 y 7, she spent 53 hours placing wooden chairs against the façade of the Palace of Justice in Bogotá, re-inhabiting the space of a violent siege. In 2003, for the 8th Istanbul Biennial, she created an installation of 1,550 wooden chairs stacked between two buildings, which she described as a “topography of war” representing mass graves and the shared experience of violence, not a specific event. In 2005, at Castello di Rivoli, she extended the gallery’s vaulted ceiling to evoke incarceration and entombment in her work Abyss. In 2007, she created Shibboleth for the Tate Modern’s Turbine Hall, a 167-metre-long crack in the floor that symbolized borders, segregation, racial hatred, and the experience of marginalized people, particularly in post-colonial societies. The crack, which began as a thin line and widened into a chasm, was designed to represent the fractures in modernity and colonialism, with Salcedo stating that the history of racism runs parallel to the history of modernity. The crack was later mended, but a sliver remained. In 2013, she created Flor de Piel, a tapestry of thousands of preserved, hand-sewn red rose petals measuring 340 cm x 500 cm, intended as a shroud for a nurse tortured to death in Colombia’s war, which was acquired by the Harvard Art Museums in 2014. Plegaria Muda, a series of two coffin-sized tables with grass growing between them, translates to “silent prayer” and reflects on gang violence and mass grave sites in Colombia. Since 1988, Salcedo has interviewed families of people “disappeared” by military forces during Colombia’s civil war and has visited abandoned villages, murder sites, and mass graves, maintaining extensive files on concentration camps, both historical and contemporary. She has consistently focused on political violence, stating that “violence defines the evils of our society.” In a 2008 interview, she noted the historical recurrence of concentration camps, from Spain’s use in Cuba in 1896 to the British in South Africa, the Germans in West Africa, and the U.S. prison system, where minor offenses like marijuana possession lead to long-term incarceration, resulting in a socially excluded underclass—what she calls “socially dead”—who are denied civil rights and participation in life.
