The town's original name derives from the Chibcha native language, where "Sa" denotes a noble title, "Ma" is a proper name, and "Cá" means a sovereign enclosure. Before the Spanish conquest of the Muisca, Samacá was a small village situated around a large lagoon known as "Lake of Cansicá" or "Valley of the Lake" (la laguna de Cansicá), surrounded by three native settlements: Patagüy, Foacá, and Sáchica. It was governed by the zaque of Hunza, and the modern town was officially founded on January 1, 1556, by Juan de los Barrios. Key economic activities include farming, cattle rearing, and mining, with primary agricultural products being potatoes, peas, corn, and beets. Coal mining is the dominant industry, and most of the coal produced is exported. Over the past decade, the local economy has experienced significant growth, and Samacá is open to international investment. Its geographic coordinates are 5°30′N 73°29′W (5.500°N 73.483°W).

The Samajwadi Janata Party (Rashtriya) (SJP(R)) was established on 5 November 1990 by Chandra Shekhar, who later served as prime minister of India from 1990 to 1991. He led the party until his death on 8 July 2007, at which time he was the party's only member in the Lok Sabha. The party was formed when Shekhar and Devi Lal split from the governing Janata Dal. The SJP(R) secured 60 MPs and formed a government with the support of the Indian National Congress (Indira), with Shekhar as prime minister, which lasted from 10 November 1990 to 21 June 1991—seven months in total—before collapsing when the Indian National Congress (Indira) withdrew its support. S. R. Bommai served as president of the Karnataka state unit of the party until the state unit merged with the Janata Dal prior to the 1994 Karnataka Assembly elections. As of 2012, Kamal Morarka, a former cabinet minister in Chandra Shekhar's union government, was the head of the party, and its headquarters were located at Narendra Niketan, ITO Indraprastha Estate, New Delhi, India.

San Roque is a town and municipality in the Colombian department of Antioquia, situated in the Northeastern Antioquia subregion at an elevation of 1,475 m (4,839 ft) above sea level. It was founded by Francisco Martinez de Ospina on 8 February 1880 and officially became a municipality in 1884. The town lies between the Nare River and the Nus River, and its establishment was driven by the presence of gold in the surrounding areas. It is located 121 km north of Medellín. San Roque celebrates most of the traditional festivals observed throughout Colombia. In 1911, the Antioquia Railway was constructed, passing near the town and contributing to the local economy, during which time San Roque functioned as a mining center. The town's historical background is a major draw for modern tourists, and it is commonly referred to as "The Land of Cordiality" due to the friendly nature of its residents. San Roque has a tropical rainforest climate (Af) characterized by heavy rainfall throughout the year. This Department of Antioquia location article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by adding missing information.

Sanduk Ruit, a Nepali ophthalmologist born on September 4, 1954, in the remote mountainous village of Olangchunggola near the Tibet border, grew up in a village of 200 people located 11,000 feet above sea level on the lap of Mt. Kanchenjunga, one of the world's most isolated regions with no electricity, schools, health facilities, or modern communication, and snow-covered for six to nine months annually. His parents, Sonam and Kesang Ruit, were rural and illiterate, and he was the second of six children; he lost three siblings—his elder brother to diarrhoea at age three and his younger sister Chundak to fever at age eight—while his younger sister Yangla, who died at 15 from tuberculosis due to poverty, deeply influenced his decision to become a doctor to serve the poor. The nearest school was fifteen days’ walk away, and at age seven, his father sent him to St Robert's School in Darjeeling, where he stayed for four to five years before returning to Nepal. He graduated from Siddhartha Vanasthali School in Kathmandu in 1969 and later earned a Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery from King George's Medical College, Lucknow, with a scholarship from 1972 to 1976. He worked as a General Physician at Bir Hospital in Kathmandu for three years before specializing in ophthalmology, earning a Master’s Degree from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Delhi, in 1984. He worked at Tripureshwor Eye Hospital for eight years and, in 1986, was mentored by Australian ophthalmologist Fred Hollows, who recognized his dedication and offered him further training in Australia, the Netherlands, and the United States. In Australia, Ruit and Hollows developed Small Incision Cataract Surgery (SICS) using intraocular lenses, and Ruit became the first Nepali doctor to use them. To make surgeries more affordable, he established the Nepal Eye Program Australia, later renamed The Fred Hollows Foundation. Despite being offered a position in Australia, he returned to Nepal and continued working at Tripureshwor. In 1994, he founded the Tilganga Eye Center, now known as the Tilganga Institute of Ophthalmology, which produces intraocular lenses at less than US $5 each and prosthetic eyes for US $3 (compared to $150 for imports), and has performed over 100,000 operations, trained over 500 medical personnel globally, and works with the Himalayan Cataract Project, co-founded with Geoff Tabin, to provide free cataract surgeries in remote areas, often using mobile eye camps in tents, classrooms, or animal stables. Ruit restored the sight of over 180,000 people across Africa and Asia using SICS. His method, which has a 98% success rate at six months, is now taught in U.S. medical schools and uses lenses that are significantly cheaper than previous ones, developed in 1995. In 2006, after treating a North Korean diplomat in Kathmandu, he was invited to North Korea, where he conducted surgery on 1,000 patients and trained local surgeons. In April 2021, he launched the Tej Kohli & Ruit Foundation with a mission to screen 1,000,000 people and cure 300,000 of cataract blindness by 2026. The foundation conducted its first microsurgical outreach camp in Lumbini in March 2021, screening 1,387 patients and curing 312 cases of blindness, and another camp in Solukhumbu in April 2021, screening 1,214 patients and curing 178 cases. Ruit was awarded the Ramon Magsaysay Award for Peace and International Understanding for placing Nepal at the forefront of developing safe, effective, and economical cataract surgery procedures, enabling the needlessly blind in poor countries to see again, and the ISA award, the highest civilian honor in Bahrain, for developing affordable and sustainable cataract treatments with a cash prize of 1 million dollars. He is referred to as the "God of Sight" after restoring the sight of a 60-year-old woman in Indonesia. His biography, *The Barefoot Surgeon* by Ali Gripper, was published in June 2018, and a Nepali translation, *Sanduk Ruit*, was released by Fine Print Books in 2019. Ruit married Nanda Shrestha, an ophthalmic nurse, in 1987 and has one son and two daughters.

Santa Rosa de Osos is a middle city and municipality in northern Antioquia, Colombia, bordered on the north by Yarumal and Angostura, on the east by Guadalupe and Carolina del Principe, on the south by Donmatías, San Pedro de los Milagros, and Entrerríos, and on the west by Belmira and San José de la Montaña. Before the Spanish arrival, the indigenous Nutabes lived in the area, known for their agility, craftsmanship in cotton, and gold extraction, with a patriarchal society and beliefs in life after death, where the dead were buried with utensils, jewelry, food, and clothing. In 1541, Spanish conquistador Francisco Vallejo discovered the region, naming it "Valley of the Bears" due to the abundance of bears, and by 1600, gold was found in abundance. In 1636, Captain Antonio Serrano y Espejo led a group of settlers to establish a settlement on the site, approved by King Philip IV of Spain. In 1659, the area became a parish under Bishop Jacinto Vasco de Contreras y Velarde and was renamed "San Jacinto de los Osos." In 1792, it was renamed "Villa de Nuestra Señora de Chiquinquirá de los Osos," and in 1811, it acquired its current name, Santa Rosa de Osos. It was officially established as a municipality in 1814 by dictator Juan del Corral. In 1917, the Diocese of Santa Rosa de Osos was created by Pope Benedicto XV, with investment from the Yarce Betancur family, one of the most powerful families at the time and founders of a local school. Bishop Miguel Angel Builes Gomez, appointed in 1924, led the diocese for over forty years and founded four religious communities: the Sisters Teresitas Comtemplativas, Teresitas Missionary Sisters, the Daughters of Our Lady of Mercy, and the Xaverian Yarumal Missionaries. Currently, Bishop Jorge Alberto Ossa Soto oversees the diocese. The municipality is known as "The City Religious" due to its strong Catholic heritage and religious tourism, featuring the Cathedral, chapels, and monuments reflecting the devotion of its people. Santa Rosa is a major producer of milk and water for the Aburrá Valley metropolitan area, supporting the construction of Lakes Riogrande I and II. Marshal Jorge Robledo arrived in Anzá in September 1541 and sent commissions, including one led by Francisco Vallejo to the "Llanos de Ovejas" (modern San Pedro de los Milagros and Entrerríos), where he discovered a cold valley named "Bear's Valley." The Nutabes resisted Spanish presence, leading Vallejo to abandon the area due to hostilities, and the region was considered poor and unprofitable, remaining neglected for nearly a century despite visits by Don Andres De Valdivia and Don Gaspar De Rodas in the mid-16th century. Early colonization began with Pedro Gutierrez Colmenero (first mayor of Medellín, 1675) and Don Antonio De Mesa, and Juan Nuño De Sotomayor discovered minerals in 1645, beginning operations in streams such as San Juan, La Trinidad, Orobajo, San Jose, San Antonio, Santa Ana, and San Lorenzo, as well as the Guadalupe River and Los Martires stream. Gutierrez Colmenero worked the mines, while Fernando Toro Zapata operated the Caruquia stream. The first village was located south of the current city, now the Arenales neighborhood, called La Rancheria in the 18th century, owned by Captain Ignacio Velez De Rivero and featuring a chapel built in 1740, linked to Catholic tradition. Rich mineral deposits near the Bramadora, San Juan, and San Antonio streams attracted many people when Antioquia's gold declined; by 1650, there were over 700 Black people and more than 500 Spaniards or their descendants working in mining, many of whom were wealthy. Mining processes were improved by Mon and Velarde, who established mining laws, and by Monsieur Laneret or Moneret, who introduced water-powered mills in the late 17th century. In the early 18th century, large immigration from Medellín and Rionegro increased the population, leading to the name change to San Jacinto de los Osos by 1770. The first priest was Juan Bautista Dávila Knight, though earlier residents included Pedro Martin de Mora and Fray Pedro Simon, who wrote about the mines. During the 18th century, five chapels existed outside the parish, including Tierradentro, and the parish chapel was dedicated to Our Lady of Guadalupe, commemorating a miracle involving Spanish adventurer Pedro Bustamante, who, harassed by natives, prayed to the Virgin and was saved by Juan Torres, who later died under attack from a native, with his body appearing to soldiers at the funeral—this story may have inspired the name Guadalupe River, though no definitive historical evidence confirms it. The village cemetery was located where today's Simon Bolivar Park, the main square, and was constructed with help from Don Pedro Rodriguez de Zea in 1775, who was governor of Los Osos and authorized the creation of Yarumal, Don Matías, and Carolina del Principe. A hidden history involves severe discrimination against Black people; despite Antioquia being one of the first regions to grant freedom to slaves, the valley remained harsh, with cruel treatment by Spaniards. Notably, Don Juan Jose Salazar and María del Pardo were known for whipping slaves and chaining them, and also for flaying cows and killing cattle in extreme pain. Salazar, who worked in the La Trinidad mine and in the area now known as Gómez Plata, was nicknamed "The Sombrerón" for wearing a large hat; after his death, residents believed he wandered through the town nightly with two large dogs, a belief that became a popular urban legend and is remembered in a street in Hoyorrico. In 1792, Governor Francisco Baraya and La Campa established the Villa, named "Village of Our Lady of the Rosary of Chiquinquirá of the Bears," marking a new mining boom with new wealthy entrepreneurs like Zulaibar replacing old elites and forming economically and culturally significant companies. Scientific advances in gold mining, especially in lode mines like Las Cruces and Las Animas, brought high returns, but gold declined quickly, leading to a shift to agriculture and livestock, improving living conditions and transforming the region into a green city with over 100 consecutive years of environmental stability and economic prosperity. The name "Santa Rosa de Osos" honors Santa Rosa de Lima and the spectacled bears that once abounded in the region. The municipality has a good population projection, driving urban development with new neighborhoods and demolition of old houses, expanding its urban perimeter and planning residential projects with services, though road and public space issues persist due to increased traffic and poor maintenance, with many streets, avenues, and parks in disrepair and lacking a central park. Public monuments and furniture such as benches, lamps, and waste bins are damaged by vandalism and neglect. Parks include those in the city and districts. Santa Rosa has a transport terminal with offices for various carriers and social services, offering daily public routes to all districts and villages, as well as to San José de la Montaña, Entrerríos, San Pedro de los Milagros, Don Matías, Carolina del Principe, and Medellín, with frequent service. Sports infrastructure includes three covered coliseums: CIC El Alto de La Mina, Minor, and Antonio Roldan Betancur, a municipal synthetic grass court, an athletic complex with a track, bicicross track, tennis court, and over 10 multisport covered courts across neighborhoods, plus open-air facilities. In Riogrande, Alto de La Mina, and St. Thomas Aquinas Seminary, there are well-equipped soccer fields. The city has excellent hotel infrastructure with diverse amenities and numerous museums, monuments, and historical buildings alongside its many churches. With a population of 36,063, the municipality has a primary care hospital and three health institutions (IPS): MEDICAL CENTER SANTA ROSA DE OSOS LTDA., CIMA HEADQUARTERS NORTH—San Juan de Dios Hospital, and IPS NORTH SAN MARCOS DE LEON S.A.S. The municipality has UNE-EDATEL for fixed telephony and internet, with excellent mobile coverage from Claro, Movistar, and Tigo. Two local radio stations, "Radio Más" and "Radio Mi Tierra," provide local information. CAPSOS, a local television company, offers over 60 channels across genres, aiming to meet community needs for information, education, and entertainment, reflecting cultural identity and creating audiovisual memory of santarosan history. It provides spaces for community voice and alternative development. In rural areas, DIRECTV is the primary television service. Electricity is provided by EPM throughout the municipality, with good public lighting coverage. The urban center has a modern domestic gas network from EPM. Water and sewer services are managed by Sustainable Water Supply and Sewerage S.A. (AASSA), with extensive drinking water coverage from the Chichi and Agua Mala (Tenche River source) streams, fed by gravity from Cerro San José and pumped from Las Cruces, forming an efficient aqueduct. Sewer systems have weaknesses: some areas lack networks and discharge directly into water sources, with community septic tanks in many places; urban streams suffer from pollution, especially Agüitas Claras, which receives 55% of untreated urban wastewater from sectors like El Hoyo, 33, Villa Cruz, and others, flowing into the Bramadora stream, and 45% goes to the Guadalupe River—12% to the Portal stream, which flows into San Jose, and 33% directly into the Guadalupe River in areas like Barro Blanco, Los Chorros, and El Turco. Wastewater from the Guadalupe River is collected by a system that reaches the Turco wastewater treatment plant, which operates within acceptable pollution standards but still visibly affects the river. Rural districts and villages have community-managed aqueducts, with basic sanitation provided by the mayor and septic tanks meeting quality standards. Some farms use water concessions or stream deposits for domestic use. The population was estimated at 37,864 in 2020, 36,103 in 2016 (19,012 urban, 17,091 rural), and literacy was 91.3% in 2005. According to DANE's 2005 census, the ethnographic composition of the municipality is detailed. The municipality has five official districts: Aragon, Hoyorrico, San Pablo, Riogrande, and San Isidro; Caney is awaiting official district status through a pending PBOT update. It has over 72 rural villages. Santa Rosa de Osos is located in the northern highlands with an average elevation of 2,550 meters above sea level, with steep slopes in San Pablo and San Isidro where elevation drops sharply to warmer thermal zones. Its total area is 812 square kilometers, of which 805 are rural and 7 urban. The territorial size is slightly larger than Kiribati and over 400 times the surface of Monaco. Coordinates: 6°39′N 75°28′W (6.650°N 75.467°W).
The coordinates are 6 degrees 39 minutes North and 75 degrees 28 minutes West, which corresponds to 6.650 degrees North and 75.467 degrees West, or 6.650; -75.467.

Santo Domingo is a town and municipality located in the Colombian department of Antioquia, situated within the Northeastern Antioquia subregion at an altitude of 1,975 meters (6,480 feet) above sea level. The municipality was established in 1778 by Don Juan Gregorio Duque, and in 1858, the writer Tomás Carrasquilla was born there. This Department of Antioquia location article is currently a stub and can be expanded with additional information on Wikipedia.

Sarah Young (March 15, 1946 – August 31, 2023) was an American author renowned for her contributions to Christian literature, particularly through her book *Jesus Calling*. She advocated for contemplative prayer and her books have sold over 45 million units worldwide, making her one of the most successful Christian authors in history. Born on March 15, 1946, in Nashville, Tennessee, Sarah Jane Kelly was the daughter of Douglass (Levine) Kelly and Tom Kelly, both educators. She graduated from E. C. Glass High School in Lynchburg, Virginia, earned a degree in philosophy from Wellesley College in 1968, and obtained a master's degree in child development from Tufts University in 1974. While in graduate school, a lapsed Christian, Young encountered the work of evangelical theologian Francis Schaeffer, whose influence significantly shaped her spiritual path. She visited L'Abri, an evangelical center in Switzerland, where she experienced a spiritual encounter and converted to Christianity. She then enrolled at Covenant Theological Seminary in Creve Coeur, Missouri, where she met her husband, Stephen Young, a third-generation missionary. They married in 1977 and served as Presbyterian missionaries near Yokkaichi, Japan for eight years, during which time Young gave birth to her two children. After Japan, the family moved to Atlanta, Georgia, where Young earned a master's degree in counseling from Georgia State University. In 1991, they relocated to Melbourne, Australia, where Young established a Christian counseling practice for women who had been sexually or spiritually abused. During meditation on God’s protection and visualization of loved ones surrounded by the Holy Spirit, she had a mystical experience in which she was enveloped by light and overwhelmed with peace. In 2001, the couple moved to Perth, where Young’s chronic health conditions—Lyme disease, melanoma, and vertigo—frequently left her housebound. In 2013, they moved to Nashville, Tennessee. Young died on August 31, 2023, from leukemia at her home in Brentwood, Tennessee, at the age of 77. Beginning in 1992, Young maintained a devotional journal in which she practiced "listening prayers," writing down what she believed God was saying to her rather than what she wanted to say. This journal eventually became the foundation of *Jesus Calling*, which was published in 2004. Initially rejected by publishers, Young abandoned publishing efforts in 2001, but her work later attracted the attention of an executive at Integrity (later part of Thomas Nelson), who offered her a contract. The book began modestly but gained widespread popularity after a renewed marketing campaign by Thomas Nelson, becoming a bestseller in Christian literature. The success of *Jesus Calling* led to the release of sequels, including *Jesus Always* and *Jesus Today*, as well as related products such as calendars, journals, children's editions, podcasts, an app, a magazine, and a television show, collectively selling over 45 million units as of August 2023. Critics, including Kathy Keller of Redeemer Presbyterian Church, Randy Alcorn of Eternal Perspective Ministries, and Tim Challies of Grace Fellowship Church, have condemned Young’s message, accusing her of blasphemy, occultic practices, paganism, panentheism, idolatry, misleading teachings, and pietism. Young was known for her intense privacy, avoiding public appearances and giving interviews only via email. She remained committed to her faith, family, and writing throughout her life. In 2009, she traveled to the United States for six months to receive treatment for Lyme disease but saw little improvement. She was survived by her husband Stephen Young, their two children Stephanie van der Westhuizen and Eric Young, her three siblings, and six grandchildren.

Sativasur is a town and municipality located in the Colombian Department of Boyacá, within the Northern Boyacá Province subregion. It is about 132 km from Tunja, the department's capital. The municipality shares borders with Sativanorte to the north, Socotá to the east, and Paz de Río to the south and west. Before the Spanish conquest of the Muisca in the central highlands (Altiplano Cundiboyacense) in 1540, both Sativasur and Sativanorte were known as Sátiva. This area was inhabited during the Herrera Period and was governed by the cacique of Tundama, now known as Duitama, which was part of the Muisca Confederation. The Spanish conquistadores who arrived in 1540 were Gonzalo Suárez Rendón and Hernán Pérez de Quesada. Sativasur was officially established on January 30, 1720. The names Sativasur and Sativanorte originate from the cacique Sátiva, whose name in the Chibcha language of the Muisca means "Captain of the Sun." The primary economic activities in the area are agriculture, livestock farming, and mining.

Savannah Churchill (born Savannah Valentine Roberts; August 21, 1920 – April 19, 1974) was an American rhythm and blues singer active in the 1940s and 1950s, best known for her number-one R&B single "I Want To Be Loved (But Only By You)." Born to Creole parents Emmett Roberts and Hazel Hickman in Colfax, Louisiana, she moved to Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, New York, with her mother Hazel Roberts and stepfather when she was three. Growing up, she played violin and sang with the choir at St. Peter Claver Catholic Church and School in Brooklyn, and later graduated from Brooklyn's Girls' High School. Her family had a house on Quincy Street that originally included a carriage house with a horse stable in the back yard. In the 1930 and 1940 United States Censuses, Churchill and her parents were listed as Negro, as Louisiana Creoles were required to do at the time; she never denied her African American ancestry and appeared in black publications such as Jet magazine. In 1939, she quit her job as a waitress to pursue a singing career, beginning at Small's Paradise in Harlem, where she earned $18 a week. She performed with the Crystal Caraverns in Washington, D.C., and then toured with the Edgar Hayes band in 1941. Her first recordings, including the risqué "Fat Meat Is Good Meat," were issued on Beacon Records in 1942, followed by recordings on Capitol with the Benny Carter Orchestra in 1943, including her first hit, "Hurry, Hurry." In 1945, she signed with Irving Berman's Manor Records, and that year "Daddy Daddy" peaked at No. 3 on the R&B chart. Two years later, she reached No. 1 on the R&B chart with "I Want To Be Loved (But Only By You)," which topped the charts for eight weeks. The record was billed as being with vocal group The Sentimentalists, who soon renamed themselves The Four Tunes. Subsequent recordings with The Four Tunes, including "Time Out For Tears" (No. 10 R&B, No. 24 pop) and "I Want To Cry," both released in 1948, were also successful. Billed as "Sex-Sational," she performed to much acclaim and appeared in the movies Miracle in Harlem (1948) and Souls of Sin (1949), both featuring African American casts. From 1949, she recorded with Regal, RCA Victor, and Decca Records, recording the original version of "Shake A Hand," later a big hit for Faye Adams, and also recording with the Ray Charles Singers. By 1952, Churchill became one of the top box-office attractions at the Apollo Theater in Harlem, the Regal Theater in Chicago, the Howard Theater in Washington, D.C., and the Palladium in London. She toured widely with backing vocal group The Striders, including a visit to Hawaii in 1954. In 1953, she released gospel tunes on Decca Records. In 1956, she was one of the first artists signed to the Argo label, set up as a subsidiary to Chess Records. Her career ended in 1956 when, while singing on stage in a club, a drunken man fell on top of her from a balcony above, causing severe, debilitating injuries from which she would never fully recover. Although she did some recording in 1960, releasing her debut album Time Out For Tears on Jamie Records, her health declined greatly until her death from pneumonia in Brooklyn in 1974. She later had two children with her first husband, David Churchill, who was killed in a car accident in 1941. On May 19, 1952, she remarried Jesse Johnson in Franklin, Ohio.

Sazae-san is a Japanese yonkoma manga series created and illustrated by Machiko Hasegawa, first published in the local paper Fukunichi Shinbun on April 22, 1946. When the Asahi Shimbun offered Hasegawa to draw the four-panel comic for their paper, she moved to Tokyo in 1949, explaining that the main characters had relocated from Kyūshū to Tokyo. The first Sazae-san strip published by the Asahi Shimbun appeared on November 30, 1949, and the manga depicted everyday life and contemporary situations in Tokyo until Hasegawa retired, with the final comic released on February 21, 1974. The series dealt with the large family dynamic in a lighthearted, easy manner, and its final episode centered on Sazae's joy over a double yolk from an egg she cracked for her husband, with Katsuo commenting on the happiness found in small life moments. As of 1999, the manga had over 86 million copies in circulation, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time, and it won the 8th Bungeishunjū Manga Award in 1962. An anime television adaptation by TCJ (later renamed Eiken) began airing in October 1969 and has remained on the air continuously, broadcasting every Sunday from 18:30 to 19:00 without change, featuring three vignettes. It holds the Guinness World Record for the longest-running animated television series, achieving the record on September 5, 2013, and as of December 2025, has aired over 9,000 episodes. The anime started as a slapstick comedy with references to Tom and Jerry and Looney Tunes but shifted to a family drama within a year, maintaining this style for over 50 years without major changes in directing, scriptwriting, or character design. The anime is considered a "national anime" in Japan with a 97% recognition rate in a 2020 NIPPON RESEARCH CENTER survey, and is seen as a symbol of universality and permanence. Despite its unchanging style, it is sometimes criticized as anachronistic due to the absence of smartphones and convenience stores, though the staff states they have no plans to update the setting to reflect modern elements. Elements like smoking and corporal punishment have been removed or addressed. The anime is not widely known outside Japan due to the rights holders' decision not to export or globally develop it, though the producer expressed hopes for future global expansion. Only Midori Katō, who voices Sazae, has never been replaced; she was recognized by Guinness World Records in 2019 for the longest career as a voice actor for the same animated character. Other main voice actors have changed: Ichirō Nagai, who played Namihei, was replaced in 2014 after his death at age 82, and Miyoko Asō, who voiced Fune, was replaced in 2015 to reflect her age at 89; Takako Sasuga, who voiced Tarao, died in 2023 at age 87 and was also replaced. Since 1974, the opening credits have introduced locations Sazae has visited in Japan, changing approximately every three months, and this has become a tourism promotion tool, with prefectures and municipalities providing 5–10 million yen in aid since 2000. From November 1991, each episode ends with a janken match between Sazae and viewers, replacing the earlier tradition of tossing a bean or rice cake in the air and catching it, which was changed due to health concerns raised by medical institutions. The anime was originally sponsored by Toshiba, which later expanded to other sponsors, though the association remained strong; when Toshiba withdrew due to poor management, it was widely reported. Sazae-san was the last animated TV series to use traditional cel animation, with the opening credits becoming digital in April 2009 and the series fully transitioning to digital animation in 2013. Hasegawa never wanted merchandise or home video rights for the series, and after her death, her request to keep older episodes from being released on home media was honored. However, in December 2018, Fuji TV partnered with Amazon Prime Video and other streaming services to release episodes from 1969 and the early-to-mid 1970s, along with some mid-2000s and mid-1990s to 2010s episodes. The opening and ending songs are original and sung by Yuko Uno, with the audio unchanged since the series began, though trimmed during early years. The series experienced two production suspensions: one for about a month in February 1975 due to the 1970s energy crisis, and another for about a month in May 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, during which past episodes were rebroadcast. In Japan, "Sazae-san syndrome" refers to a depressed mood on Sunday night after watching the show, signaling the end of the weekend. In 1955, a radio station aired a serial drama based on the comic, and a short-lived live-action TV series aired on what is now TBS. In November 1965, TBS launched a dramatic series modeled after the manga, which aired until September 1967. In 1979, NHK produced a six-month dramatic serial focusing on the creation of Sazae-san and Machiko Hasegawa. In 2010, Fuji Television launched a live-action situation comedy, Sazae-san 2, followed by Sazae-san 3 the next year, using the same elements including the theme music and closing janken match. In 2008, Glico featured the family in "25 years later" commercials for its "Otona Glico" chocolates, with actors Eita (Tarao), Tadanobu Asano (Katsuo), Rie Miyazawa (Wakame), and Shun Oguri (Ikura). In 2017, Sazae and Masao appeared in a Cup Noodles commercial drawn by Katsuya Kondō.

Severance is an American science fiction psychological thriller television series created by Dan Erickson and executive produced and primarily directed by Ben Stiller. It stars Adam Scott, Zach Cherry, Britt Lower, Tramell Tillman, Jen Tullock, Dichen Lachman, Michael Chernus, John Turturro, Christopher Walken, Patricia Arquette, and Sarah Bock. The series follows employees at Lumon Industries, a biotechnology corporation, who have undergone "severance"—a procedure that splits a person's memories between work and their personal life, creating two separate identities: the "innie," who has no knowledge of the outside world, and the "outie," who lives their life outside without knowing about their job. Erickson and Stiller first developed the series in 2015, with Apple TV+ greenlighting it in 2019, attaching Scott to the lead role. The first season cast was finalized by December 2020, and the second season cast was announced in October 2022. Principal photography took place in New York, New Jersey, and Newfoundland. The first season aired from February 18 to April 8, 2022, and the second season from January 17 to March 21, 2025. The series has been renewed for a third season. Severance has received critical acclaim for its cinematography, direction, production design, musical score, story, and performances, earning 41 Primetime Emmy Award nominations, including wins for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series (Britt Lower) and Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series (Tramell Tillman). Adam Scott received nominations for a Primetime Emmy Award, two Television Critics Association Awards, and a Golden Globe Award, while Stiller and Erickson earned Emmy nominations for directing and writing. Ben Stiller has an uncredited voice cameo as an animated version of Kier Eagan in season 1, and Keanu Reeves has an uncredited voice cameo as an animated Lumon building in a Lumon industrial film in season 2. Episodes in season 2 were promoted as being released on Fridays globally from January 17, but aired in American time zones on the preceding Thursday evenings. Erickson conceived the series during a period of depression while working an office job at a door factory after completing his master's degree in television writing, describing the job as monotonous and wishing he could "skip the eight hours of the workday, to disassociate and just get it over with." He submitted his pilot script to Ben Stiller's production company Red Hour Productions in 2015, which was passed to Stiller by Jackie Cohn and Nicholas Weinstock. Stiller read the script at least five years before the premiere and called it "the longest thing I've ever worked on," noting his enjoyment of its contributions to workplace comedy. Erickson described earlier versions of the pilot as "weirder" with elements like a disembodied pair of legs running by Mark, a charred floor with burnt desks, and a woman trapped in a glass cubicle, and credited Stiller with grounding the show by avoiding excessive surrealism. Stiller said he fell in love with the "weird human sadness" of a person willingly undergoing the procedure. In November 2019, Apple TV+ gave the series a series order with Stiller directing and Scott in the lead role. Stiller initially directed only the pilot but later directed more episodes. On April 6, 2022, Apple renewed the series for a second season. In April 2023, Beau Willimon was hired as an executive producer and writer for the second and potential third seasons. On March 21, 2025, shortly after the season 2 finale premiere, Apple announced a renewal for a third season. The Writers Guild of America West database lists Eli Jorne and Mary Laws as new showrunners for the third season, replacing Chris Black and Mark Friedman, who showran the first two seasons alongside Erickson. Media influences include the Backrooms creepypasta, The Stanley Parable (2013), Office Space, The Truman Show, Being John Malkovich, Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, the Black Mirror episode "White Christmas," and Dilbert. Older influences include the existential hell in Jean-Paul Sartre's 1944 play No Exit and the totalitarian dystopia in George Orwell's 1949 novel Nineteen Eighty-Four. Aesthetically, the series was influenced by Brazil, Dark City, and Playtime. Erickson's siblings inspired some characters. In 2016, his pilot screenplay appeared on Blood List's survey of the best unproduced genre screenplays. Erickson stated that the show was born from frustrations with workplace demands, noting that employees are expected to give endlessly with no meaningful return. In January 2017, Stiller invited Adam Scott to star; they had previously worked together in Stiller's 2013 film The Secret Life of Walter Mitty. Stiller intended to appear as a doctor in the first season but scrapped the role, saying it didn't feel right and that he's happy to be off-camera. In January 2020, Patricia Arquette, Britt Lower, Jen Tullock, and Zach Cherry were added to the cast; Tramell Tillman joined in February 2020, and John Turturro and Christopher Walken were added in November 2020. Dichen Lachman was cast in December 2020. Turturro recommended Walken for the role of Burt because he had known him for a long time and didn't need to act like friends. On October 31, 2022, Gwendoline Christie, Bob Balaban, Merritt Wever, Alia Shawkat, Robby Benson, Stefano Carannante, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson, and John Noble joined the cast for season 2. Stiller offered former U.S. President Barack Obama a voice cameo in season 2, but he declined; the role went to Keanu Reeves. Production designer Jeremy Hindle blended corporate aesthetics from the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s, citing modernist architect Eero Saarinen as influential for the building design. This included the John Deere World Headquarters in Moline, Illinois, and the Bell Labs Holmdel Complex in New Jersey, both designed as "work designed to do work," which served as both exterior and ground floor interiors for Lumon Industries. Set designs from Playtime also inspired internal sets. Main sets were created on soundstages in The Bronx: one soundstage featured around 140 feet (43 m) of hallway that was rearranged to create a maze-like structure, and another larger hallway was used in later episodes of season 1. A second soundstage was used for main rooms like the Macrodata Refinement Division, designed to create a feeling of being trapped with a large room (80 by 40 feet or 24 m × 12 m) and low ceiling. Hindle described this room as a playroom for new hires, with green carpeting to resemble grass. Other Lumon spaces were inspired by M.C. Escher. Erickson said the mix of cars and technologies from different eras was meant to "give a slight sense of disorientation" and make Lumon "feel unmoored from time and space." The production team sourced 400 anachronistic cars, mostly boxy 1980s and 1990s vehicles in good condition, each intentionally placed to create a retro science fiction aesthetic. Characters' vehicles include Mark's Volvo S90, Cobel's Volkswagen Rabbit, Helena's Lincoln Continental, and Milchick's Royal Enfield motorcycle. All office equipment carries Lumon branding. Prop designers reconstructed old computers with functional trackball devices so actors could perform the work shown, and the computers lack an escape key as a metaphor for the innies' lack of control. The terminals were modeled after 1970s Data General Dasher terminals, with keycaps recreated by Signature Plastics, who also made the original keycaps. The keycap set was re-released in 2025 under the name "SA Macrodata Refinement." The COVID-19 pandemic delayed the initial production start in March 2020. First season filming began in New York City under the working title Tumwater on November 8, 2020, with the opening scene shot on January 6, 2021. Filming occurred in Nyack, New York (for Mark and Cobel's homes), Kingston and Beacon, New York (in March), and moved to central New Jersey in April, primarily at the Bell Labs Holmdel Complex, which stood in for Lumon HQ. Filming was scheduled to conclude on June 23, 2021. Second season filming began on October 3, 2022, in New York City, with a planned wrap date of May 12, 2023. However, production was shut down on May 8, 2023, due to the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike. It resumed on May 13, 2023, in Newfoundland, was shut down again due to both strikes, and resumed on January 29, 2024, wrapping on April 23, 2024. In 2025, Severance became the most watched series in Apple TV+ history. Both seasons received critical acclaim: on Rotten Tomatoes, the overall series holds a 96% approval rating, with the first season at 97% (based on 117 reviews, average 8.5/10) and the second season at 94% (based on 223 reviews). The consensus for season 1 is: "Audacious, mysterious, and bringing fresh insight into the perils of corporate drudgery, Severance is the complete package." Metacritic gives the series an 85 out of 100, with season 1 at 83 and season 2 at 86, both indicating "universal acclaim." Reviews from Lucy Mangan (The Guardian) and Rachael Sigee (I) gave it five out of five stars, Huw Fullerton (Radio Times), John Nugent (Empire), Alan Sepinwall (Rolling Stone), and Anita Singh (The Telegraph) gave it four out of five, and Patrick Ryan (USA Today) gave it 3.5 out of 4. Mangan praised Stiller's direction, writing, and performances (especially Arquette, Turturro, Walken, and Tillman). Sigee praised the performances and called the series "original, weird, thought-provoking and beautifully crafted." Fullerton praised Scott's performance and called it "an impressive creation." Nugent praised the direction, performances of Scott, Arquette, Turturro, and Walken, and their chemistry. Sepinwall praised Stiller's direction, cast performances (notably Scott, Turturro, Walken, Lower, and Tillman), production design, tone, and season finale. Carly Lane (Collider) and Ben Travers (IndieWire) graded it an "A," with Travers noting the series "plays out cleanly and efficiently" and "knows how to make the most of its episodic format." Stephen Robinson (The A.V. Club) gave it an "A-" and praised Stiller's direction and the cast, highlighting Lower, Scott, Tillman, Turturro, Walken, Tullock, and Cherry. Kristen Baldwin (Entertainment Weekly) gave it a "B+" and highlighted Scott, Lower, and Tillman, calling Scott a "superb fit" and noting Lower's vulnerability and Tillman's charisma. Samantha Nelson (IGN) gave it a 9 out of 10, saying it sets up an intriguing mystery with room for character evolution. Shane Ryan (Paste) gave it an 8.1 out of 10, praising Scott, Arquette, and Tillman, as well as Stiller and McArdle's direction. Kyle Mullin (Under the Radar) gave it an 8 out of 10, calling it a "Golden Age of TV gem" and noting Stiller's strong direction in workplace scenes. The American Film Institute named it one of the ten best television programs of the year. The first season received The ReFrame Stamp for hiring people of underrepresented gender identities and of color. The second season has a 94% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a consensus: "Masterfully managing its two halves of adroit character study and surreal nightmare, Severance's long-awaited sophomore season makes cognitive dissonance a mind-melting pleasure." Alison Herman (Variety) gave season 2 a perfect rating, noting it "fulfills this sine qua non with deceptive ease." John Nugent (Empire) gave season 2 four stars, saying it expands and deepens original mysteries while opening new ones. For its first season, the series received 7 major nominations at the 74th Primetime Emmy Awards and 7 additional nominations at the 74th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards, including Outstanding Drama Series, Adam Scott for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series, John Turturro and Christopher Walken for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series, Patricia Arquette for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series, Ben Stiller for Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series, and Dan Erickson for Outstanding Writing for a Drama Series.

The second season of Severance received a rating of 86 out of 100 based on 43 critics, indicating "universal acclaim." Writing for Variety, Alison Herman awarded the season a perfect rating, stating: "Season 2 fulfills this sine qua non with deceptive ease. Real-time viewers have had their patience strained; future binge-watchers will barely notice a blip." John Nugent of Empire gave the season 4 stars out of 5, noting: "After a storming Season One, Season Two expands and deepens the original mysteries while opening up new ones. Sharply made and skilfully executed, the employee benefits are there if you stay with it." The series received 10 major nominations for the 77th Primetime Emmy Awards and 17 additional nominations for the 77th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards, making it the most-nominated series at both ceremonies. It won three acting awards: Britt Lower for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series, Tramell Tillman for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series, and Merritt Wever for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series, as well as five awards in technical categories. Notable nominations included Outstanding Drama Series, Adam Scott for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series, Zach Cherry and John Turturro for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series, Jessica Lee Gagné and Ben Stiller for Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series, and Dan Erickson for Outstanding Writing for a Drama Series. The second season was teased during the Apple Event on September 7, 2022, which featured Helly (Britt Lower). The first footage from season 2 was released on June 10, 2024, as part of a promo for upcoming Apple TV+ programming. On July 9, 2024, a post on the Apple TV+ account on social media platform X teased an announcement about season 2, featuring a light blinking the word "tomorrow" in Morse code. The next day, on July 10, Apple TV+ announced that season 2 would debut on January 17, 2025. The first trailer for season 2 was released on October 23, 2024. On January 14, 2025, three days before the premiere, Apple TV+ recreated the show's 'Macrodata Refinement' office inside a glass box at Grand Central Terminal, where actors Scott, Cherry, Arquette, Lower, and Tillman entered and performed their roles for about two and a half hours, generating largely favorable public responses. On March 21, 2025, IKEA India and Australia posted the same advertisement promoting office supplies that replicated the Macrodata Refinement setup, using a tagline that pokes fun at the "mysterious and important work" joke made by office workers. On March 26, 2025, cast members Adam Scott, Britt Lower, Tramell Tillman, Zach Cherry, and Gwendoline Christie appeared at Tower Bridge in London to celebrate the renewal of season 3, with balloons featuring Adam Scott's face. On the same day, Apple updated its computer section on its website to include the Lumon Terminal Pro, which was not for sale but served as marketing to promote both the show and the Apple TV+ service. The official release dates of second-season episodes were on Fridays, but Apple TV+ released episodes the prior Thursday at 9:00 pm ET. The first season was released in the UK on Blu-ray and DVD on December 2, 2024, in Australia on December 4, 2024, and in the United States on December 17, 2024. An epistolary novel titled Severance: The Lexington Letter, released by Apple Books, purports to be a "tell-all" exposé of sinister occurrences at Lumon Corporation, presented as a dialogue between former Lumon employee Margeret "Peg" Kincaid and her innie (work self), sent as a letter to a Topeka newsletter. A fictional self-help book, The You You Are, was released by Apple Books as an e-book and audiobook, the latter read by actor Michael Chernus in his role as Ricken Hale. The official Severance podcast premiered in January 2025, hosted by Ben Stiller and Adam Scott, with each episode recapping a series episode and featuring interviews with an actor, crew member, or fan of the show.

Shah Faesal, born on 17 May 1983 in the Sogam area of Lolab Valley, Kupwara district, Jammu and Kashmir, is an Indian bureaucrat currently serving as Deputy Secretary in the Ministry of Culture (India) and previously in the Union Ministry for Tourism. His father, Ghulam Rasool Shah, was a teacher killed by militants in 2002 when Faesal was 19; his mother, Mubeena Shah, and grandfather were also teachers. Faesal graduated in 2008 from Jhelum Valley Medical College and earned an MBBS from Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences (SKIMS), Srinagar, completing his medical degree at age 26. He holds a master's degree in Urdu and was a gold medalist at SKIMS during his medical studies. In 2009, he secured Rank 1 in the UPSC civil services examination, becoming the first Kashmiri to top it and the first from Kashmir in several years to be selected to the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) through open merit. He was also the fourth Muslim (after Independence) to achieve this rank. Faesal was appointed assistant commissioner, revenue, of Pulwama district on 16 August 2012, transferred to deputy commissioner of Bandipora on 8 February 2014, and later served as Director School Education, Kashmir, from 22 August 2015 until 18 October 2016, when Ajaz Ahmad Bhat took over. He was temporarily given additional charge of the vice-chairman of J&K Lakes and Waterways Development Authority on 26 March 2016. In May 2018, he was transferred to the J&K State Power Development Corporation as managing director, later asked to remain in his post, and received the Fulbright-Nehru Masters' Fellowship in May 2018 to study at the Harvard Kennedy School. On 9 January 2019, he tendered his resignation from the IAS via a Facebook post, citing "unabated killings" in Kashmir and disillusionment with his role, including jailing people and imposing curfews, which the central government reportedly rejected and he later withdrew. On 4 February 2019, he began his political life with a public speech in Kupwara, where he compared his IAS experience to spending 10 years in jail. On 25 February 2019, he announced during a live NDTV debate that he was launching a political party and had applied to the Election Commission. On 16 March 2019, he announced the formation of the Jammu and Kashmir People's Movement (JKPM) on 17 March at a football ground in Rajbagh, Srinagar, stating it would provide a platform for youth and veteran politicians with a clean image. The party did not contest the 2019 Indian general election and focused on outreach, emphasizing the protection of Article 370 and Article 35A of the Indian Constitution. On 18 June 2019, he and Engineer Rashid announced a political alliance called the Peoples United Front with the Awami Ittehad Party, advocating for the resolution of the Kashmir dispute based on Kashmiri wishes, peaceful India-Pakistan relations, protection of the state's special status, return of Kashmiri Pandits, and release of detained politicians. Faesal was detained on 14 August 2019 while attempting to fly to Turkey, taken into preventive detention first at the Centaur Hotel and later at the MLA hostel, where he remained for six months. He filed a habeas corpus plea in the Delhi High Court in August 2019, claiming he was going to the U.S. for studies and had been illegally detained; the government argued he lacked a student visa and had provoked protests, and claimed he refused to guarantee he would not repeat such actions. The plea was withdrawn by his wife in September 2019. He was booked under the Public Safety Act (PSA) in February 2020, accused of subtly advocating separatism, with the detention extended by three months on 13 May, and revoked on 3 June 2020, after a 10-month detention, followed by immediate house arrest. He was reinstated in the Indian Administrative Service in April 2022 and posted as Deputy Secretary in the Union Ministry for Tourism in August 2022. On 10 August 2020, JKPM announced that Faesal had decided to exit politics and requested to be relieved from the party, which complied, with Chairman Javaid Mustafa Mir appointed as his replacement. Faesal has written for the Greater Kashmir newspaper and participated in the Jammu & Kashmir Right to Information movement with Dr. Raja Muzaffar Bhat. He made bold social media posts, including a tweet in July 2018 stating "Population +patriarchy +illiteracy +alcohol +porn +technology +anarchy = rapistan," which he clarified was not about India, though disciplinary action was taken by both the J&K and central governments. During the 2016 Kashmir unrest, he urged national media not to use his image in comparison with Burhan Wani, threatening to resign if such comparisons continued. In 2019, Hizbul Mujahideen circulated a poster warning about Faesal. In February 2019, the Ministry of Home Affairs withdrew security cover from 155 people in Jammu and Kashmir, including Faesal. On 14 August 2019, he was stopped at IGI Airport while attempting to travel to Turkey and returned to Kashmir. He has named both Prime Minister Imran Khan and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal as role models. Mani Shankar Aiyar wrote an article titled "Kashmir's Arvind Kejriwal" about Faesal. On 3 March 2019, he recommended the Nobel Peace Prize for Imran Khan for "saving South Asia from a nuclear catastrophe." During a talk at the India International Center in February 2019, he described Kashmir as a "High Altitude Graveyard," advocating for "humanising the discourse" and urging people not to view the Kashmir issue as merely a "law and order problem." On 5 March 2021, he tweeted, "Friends let’s sort it out for once. I have always been pro-India. But now I am single-mindedly, shamelessly, helplessly and unapologetically pro-India. I stick to my side. It is a long story and I have to tell this story one day. But this is how it is going to be. Peace." Shah Faesal is married to Iram Rashid, an officer of the KAS, and has a son named Jami Faesal.

Shai, an American vocal R&B/soul quartet that gained prominence in the 1990s, formed on the campus of Howard University, influenced by the vocal styles of Boyz II Men, Jodeci, and Color Me Badd. The group was initially composed of Alpha Phi Alpha fraternity brothers Marc Gay, Carl Martin, and Darnell Van Rensalier, who invited fellow Howard University student Garfield Bright to join after two founding members left; none of the members had professional singing experience and primarily performed on campus for fun. They came together seriously after winning a Howard University talent show and decided to pursue a record deal in New York City, though they did not receive any offers. Martin gave Paco Lopez, a local deejay at WPGC radio in the DC metro, a demo cassette of "If I Ever Fall in Love," which he began promoting on the air. In September 1992, the group signed with Gasoline Alley/MCA Records and released their debut album later that year. The single "If I Ever Fall in Love," released as the first track from the debut album of the same name, peaked at number two on the Billboard Hot 100 and sold over two million copies. The subsequent singles "Comforter" and "Baby I'm Yours" each reached number 10 on the U.S. charts. At the group's insistence, the "Baby I'm Yours" music video was filmed on the Howard University campus, featuring actual Howard students, including future television host and model Ananda Lewis, as female love interests. Their next album, Right Back at Cha, was a remix album consisting mostly of new versions of their earlier hits and a few new songs, including a reworked version of "Baby I'm Yours" titled "Yours," which reached US No. 63. In 1993, Shai won an NAACP Image Award for Outstanding New Artist and performed at Bill Clinton's inauguration alongside Michael Jackson, Quincy Jones, Ray Charles, and Diana Ross. The group also appeared on The Arsenio Hall Show and The Tonight Show. In early 1994, they made a guest appearance on the sitcom "Family Matters" in the episode "Good Cop, Bad Cop" during a dream sequence. They released "The Place Where You Belong" from the Beverly Hills Cop III soundtrack, which was their final Top 40 single, peaking at No. 32 on the R&B chart. In late 1995, their follow-up album Blackface was released, reaching No. 42 on the Pop chart and No. 15 on the R&B chart; it included their final R&B Top 20 single "Come with Me," which reached US No. 43. The 1996 remix "I Don't Wanna Be Alone," featuring Jay-Z, peaked at No. 89 on the U.S. charts and was inspired by Belinda Carlisle's "Heaven Is a Place on Earth." The 2001 single "Song For You" by Rick Braun, featuring Shai, reached No. 39 on the R&B chart. As of 2025, Shai continues to perform together in various concerts and shows.

A 22-year-old photojournalist in Mumbai was gang-raped by five individuals, including a juvenile, on 22 August 2013, at the deserted Shakti Mills compound near Mahalaxmi in South Mumbai. She had gone on an assignment with a male colleague, and the accused tied up the colleague, raped the photojournalist, and used a broken beer bottle to hold her down, taking photos of her during the assault and threatening to release them online if she reported the crime. The perpetrators forced her to clean the scene and later brought her and her colleague to railway tracks around 7:15 pm, instructing them to stay. After the attackers left, the victim informed her colleague of being raped six times and needed medical help. They reached Mahalaxmi station, where her colleague contacted their boss and they went to Jaslok Hospital at Peddar Road. The victim, who was bleeding heavily, was admitted and began treatment. She gave a statement to police on 26 August and was discharged on 27 August. In a hospital statement, she expressed her desire for no other woman to face such humiliation, called for severe punishment, and stated she would continue fighting and return to work. Nirmala Samant Prabhawalkar of the National Commission for Women noted she was recovering but still traumatized. On 3 September, a 19-year-old telephone operator reported being gang-raped at the same Shakti Mills compound by five men on 31 July 2013, three of whom were also involved in the photojournalist case. Similar to the first incident, the attackers tied and beat the victim’s male companion before raping her, and the two victims fled to Chhattisgarh without reporting the crime due to fear. Mumbai Police conducted a "two-finger test" on the telephone operator despite a Maharashtra Government Resolution of 10 May 2013 that banned the test as degrading and medically irrelevant. Police formed 20 teams and involved officers from 12 crime branch units and 16 police stations. The five accused in the photojournalist case—Vijay Jadhav, Siraj Rehman Khan alias Sirju, Chand Shaikh, Mohamed Kasim Hafiz Sheikh alias Kasim, and Mohammed Salim Ansari—were arrested within 65 hours of the complaint being registered. Chand Shaikh was arrested on 23 August from Dhobi Ghat, Vijay Jadhav on 24 August from a video club, Siraj Rehman Khan on 24 August from a hideout in Govandi, Qasim Shaikh on 25 August outside Nair Hospital, and Salim Ansari on 25 August at the Delhi-Haryana border after fleeing to Delhi. The accused in the telephone operator case included Vijay Jadhav, Mohamed Kasim Hafiz Sheikh, Mohammed Salim Ansari, Mohammed Ashfaq Sheikh (26), and an unnamed minor. On 19 September 2013, the Mumbai crime branch filed charges against the four adults and a minor, including sections 376(d) for gang rape, 377 for unnatural offence, 120(b) for criminal conspiracy, 342 and 343 for wrongful restraint, 506(2) for criminal intimidation, 34 for common intention, and 201 for destruction of evidence. The prosecution also sought a charge under section 67A of the Information Technology Act against Ansari for showing porn clips to the survivor. The sessions court, presided over by Principal Sessions Judge Shalini Phansalkar-Joshi, ordered trial to begin on 14 October 2013 and was to be completed within 60 days. On 14 October, three independent witnesses testified; the photojournalist’s mother and boss gave statements, and the proceedings were held in-camera on the second and third days. On 17 October, the photojournalist identified her attackers in a four-hour deposition. On 30 October, the telephone operator testified, weeping and trembling, and recognized four of the five accused. On 20 November, her friend testified. On 13 January 2014, the photojournalist’s male colleague testified and identified all accused. On 20 March 2014, the sessions court convicted all five adult accused on 13 counts, including gang rape, destruction of evidence, wrongful restraint, assault, common intention, unnatural sex, criminal conspiracy, and charges under the Information Technology Act. The court awarded the death penalty to Vijay Jadhav, Qasim Shaikh, and Salim Ansari—repeat offenders in both cases—on 4 April 2014, marking the first time in India that such a sentence was given under section 376E of the IPC, introduced after the 2012 Delhi gang rape. Siraj Khan, the other convicted in the photojournalist case, was sentenced to life imprisonment. The judge emphasized the depravity of the accused, stating they enjoyed the assault, had no motive, and showed no remorse, and that the crime was premeditated and heinous. The court rejected arguments based on socioeconomic status or lack of physical injuries, noting the trauma and the need for deterrence. On 25 November 2021, the Bombay High Court commuted the death sentences of the three repeat offenders to life imprisonment. A division bench of Justices Sadhana Jadhav and Prithviraj Chavan ruled that section 376E is not a substantive offence but a punishment for repeat offenders under sections 376D, 376DA, and 376DB, and that death penalty is not mandatory. The court stated that death ends the possibility of repentance and that while the crime is heinous, it does not necessarily warrant the death penalty.

Jadhav and Prithviraj Chavan ruled that while setting aside the death penalty, it might appear to the public that the court is acting against the majority, but constitutional courts must follow established legal procedures rather than focusing solely on individual rights or the rights of the accused. They clarified that Section 376E of the Indian Penal Code is not a standalone substantive offence but a punishment for repeat offenders under Sections 376D, 376DA, and 376DB, and not necessarily for committing an offence after the first conviction as per Section 75 of the Indian Penal Code, but rather for cases tried after a prior conviction for a similar offence. The court noted that death penalty eliminates the possibility of repentance or mental suffering. Although acknowledging the heinous nature of the offence, the court stated that it cannot be assumed the accused deserve only the death penalty. Instead, it held that the convicts deserve rigorous imprisonment for life—meaning the remainder of their natural lives—without any remission, parole, or furlough, as their conduct, including their bold confession to the survivor that she was not the first victim, shows no possibility of reformation or rehabilitation. The court concluded that such individuals should not be reintegrated into society, as they view women with contempt, derision, and as objects of desire. Samajwadi Party (SP) MLA Naresh Agarwal (now in BJP) sparked controversy over the Mumbai gang-rape by suggesting women should pay attention to their clothing to avoid being raped and that they should not be overly influenced by television. In response to the verdict, the mother of the telephone operator stated that the convicts deserved death, as no harsher punishment would be fitting, and that their release would encourage further crimes and send a wrong message to society. She emphasized that equal urgency must be applied to all rape and molestation cases and shared how the incident has deeply affected her life, with neighbors taunting her and youths chasing her, especially during family outings. She also noted that the quick conviction was due to the proximity of the 2014 general elections. On 10 April 2014, SP chief Mulayam Singh Yadav said that when boys and girls have differences, the girl's statement that "the boy raped me" leads to the boy receiving a death sentence, and in reference to the Mumbai gang rape, he stated that after differences arose, the girl reported the rape, resulting in three men being sentenced to death. He claimed that rape cases should not lead to hanging, as boys make mistakes, and that two or three had been given death sentences in Mumbai. Complaints were filed against Yadav with the Election Commission and the National Commission for Women (NCW). His comments were denounced by the Indian media, women's groups, women's rights activists, public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam in the Shakti Mills case, Bollywood celebrities, and many Uttar Pradesh residents. The Times of India criticized Yadav as having sunk to a new low, stating that the legal changes were the result of citizens' efforts to transform India's social outlook, and that calling rape a "mistake boys make" was a direct insult to those efforts. The parents of the 2012 Delhi gang rape victim strongly condemned Yadav, urging people not to vote for his party, with the victim's mother stating that rape is a crime, not a mistake, and that a leader making such remarks has no right to power. The remarks were criticized by both BJP and Congress politicians, some of whom demanded an apology from Yadav. Rashtriya Janata Dal President Lalu Prasad Yadav criticized Yadav, saying he had lost his mental balance and that there is no place for rapists in society. Political leaders like Raj Thackeray and Prime Minister candidate Narendra Modi condemned Yadav for his insensitive and anti-women views during appearances on Aap Ki Adalat. Mulayam was defended by his daughter-in-law Dimple Yadav, who stated such comments are made by many people and happen occasionally. Following a gang rape in Budaun district on 27 May 2014, United Nations Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon criticized Yadav, stating that the "boys will be boys" attitude is dismissive and destructive. After Yadav's comments, he and several SP leaders were labeled as "Supporters of Rape and Rapists". The day after Yadav's remarks, SP Maharashtra unit chief Abu Azmi told Mid-Day that any woman, whether married or unmarried, who goes along with a man with or without consent should be hanged, as rape is punishable by hanging in Islam, and that in this case, women are also guilty. He claimed that girls complain when touched, even when not touched, and that if rape occurs with or without consent, it should be punished as per Islamic law. He also said that he did not know the context of Yadav's statement, but that the wrong people are sometimes given the death penalty, and that boys commit such acts in "josh" (excitement), and that the death sentence should be given, adding that he would not speak against Islam. Azmi's comments were widely criticized across India.

Shanice Lorraine Wilson-Knox (born May 14, 1973) is an American singer, songwriter, record producer, and actress known for her five-octave coloratura soprano voice. Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, she was raised by her mother, Crystal Wilson, a singer, and her father, Carl Black, a guitarist; after their divorce in 1979, she moved to Los Angeles with her mother and aunt Penni Wilson. At age nine, she appeared in a commercial with Ella Fitzgerald for Kentucky Fried Chicken. In 1984, she competed on Star Search, the largest national talent show at the time, winning the Junior Vocalist category with performances of "Somewhere Over the Rainbow" and "Greatest Love of All," earning a $5,000 prize. That same year, she joined the cast of Kids Incorporated and performed in the Westwood Playhouse musical Get Happy. John McClain from A&M Records saw her perform and signed her at age eleven. Her debut album, Discovery, released on October 21, 1987, peaked at number 149 on the US Billboard 200; its singles "(Baby Tell Me) Can You Dance" and "No 1/2 Steppin'" became top-ten R&B hits, with the former reaching number fifty on the US Billboard Hot 100. Due to challenges in marketing her as a young artist, she was released from A&M Records. In 1990, she signed with Motown Records and released her second album, Inner Child, internationally on November 19, 1991, which peaked at number eighty-three on the Billboard 200 and number thirteen on the US Top R&B Albums chart. The lead single, "I Love Your Smile," reached number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 and became a number-one hit in several countries, earning a nomination for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance at the 35th Annual Grammy Awards in 1993. The album also produced "I'm Cryin'" (number eleven on the US Hot R&B Singles) and "Silent Prayer" (number thirty-one on the Billboard Hot 100 and number four on the R&B chart), which featured Johnny Gill. Inner Child received a gold certification from the RIAA on May 26, 1992. The single "Saving Forever for You," released on the Beverly Hills, 90210 soundtrack in October 1992, peaked at number four on the US Billboard Hot 100. In July 1993, "It's for You" from The Meteor Man soundtrack reached number fifty-five on the Billboard Hot 100. In June 1994, she released her third album, 21... Ways to Grow, which had initial chart success with "Somewhere" and "Turn Down the Lights" peaking in the top thirty on the US Hot R&B Singles chart, but ultimately became a commercial failure; its final singles "I Like" and "I Wish" had little chart impact. Following the album's poor sales and her release from Motown, she went on a five-year hiatus. During this time, she provided background vocals for several chart-topping songs, including "Un-Break My Heart" and "When You Believe," and contributed to Toni Braxton's Secrets (1996) and Usher's My Way (1997). In January 1997, she made her theater debut as Eponine in the Broadway production of Les Misérables. In 1997, she signed with Arista Records but moved to LaFace Records at the request of co-owner LA Reid. In March 1999, she released her self-titled fourth album on LaFace Records, with the lead single "When I Close My Eyes" moving from number 91 to number 16 on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number 12—setting a then-record milestone. Album sales declined after the release of the second single "Yesterday," and in August 1999, she toured as the opening act for NSYNC's Boys of Summer Tour. In 2000, she was dropped from LaFace Records after becoming pregnant with her first child. After appearing in the movie One Special Moment in June 2001, she went on another music hiatus and made a guest appearance in One on One's season one episode "Me & My Shadow." In 2005, she released the single "Every Woman Dreams," which peaked at number 62 on the US R&B chart, and in February 2006, released her fifth studio album Every Woman Dreams on her own record label Imajah Records, which she founded in 2005, named after her children Imani and Elijah. The album peaked at number thirty on the US Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart, with singles "Take Care of U" and "So Sexy" reaching within the top seventy on the US Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart. In 2010, she performed vocals on "Behind the Mask" from Michael Jackson's posthumous album Michael and recorded "A Midnight Rendezvous" for the 2012 Kinect game Rhythm Party and "Love Is the Gift" for the video game The Bouncer. In November 2014, the Oprah Winfrey Network aired the reality television series Flex & Shanice, which ran for three seasons and chronicled her life with her husband and their family; to coincide with the show's debut, she released "Gotta Blame Me" and "We Can Fly," followed by "Another Lonely Day in California" in July 2015 and "Breakdown" in 2016. In 2019, she released "He Won't," in 2022 recorded the theme song for the animated children's series Mecha Builders, and in September 2025 starred as former First Lady Michelle Obama in the Off-Broadway production of 44: The Obama Musical. In November 2025, she announced her appearance in the BET+ Christmas movie A Soulful Christmas. Her musical influences include The Emotions, Minnie Riperton, The Clark Sisters, Stevie Wonder, and Teena Marie; she recorded a cover of Riperton's "Lovin' You" on both Inner Child (1991) and Every Woman Dreams (2006) and cited MC Lyte as her favorite rapper, influencing the rap verse on "I Love Your Smile." In November 2018, she launched her beauty line Smile by Shanice, featuring cruelty-free and vegan lipsticks and lip glosses. On February 19, 2000, she married actor and comedian Flex Alexander, with whom she has two children: daughter Imani Knox (2001) and son Elijah Knox (2004). In 2024, she revealed a breast cancer diagnosis and underwent a double mastectomy. Her voice has been described as a coloratura soprano with the ability to sing in falsetto and whistle register. Music critics have noted her strong vocal talent but have also suggested she deserves better songwriting and more creative material. The Grammy Awards, presented annually by the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences, recognize outstanding achievements in music, while the Soul Train Music Awards honor excellence in Black music and entertainment.

The Shastri Nagar metro station, previously known as Vivekanandapuri, is situated on the Red Line of the Delhi Metro. There are ATMs available at the station, though specific details about them are not provided. The station is located one and a half hours away from Nehru Place.
